G4500.d:
ῥοιζηδόν 
 adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow), 
with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2 Pet.3:10.†
 (AS)

G4501.d:
ῥομφαία, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב ;] 
a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: Rev.1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21; metaphorically, Luke.2:35.†
 (AS)

G4502.d:
Ῥουβήν, ὁ indecl., (Heb. רְאוּבֵן), 
 Reuben: Rev.7:5.†
 (AS)

G4503.d:
Ῥoύθ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רוּת), 
 Ruth: Matt.15:1-39.†
 (AS)

G4505.d:
ῥύμη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Isa.15:3 (רְחֹב), Pro.31:23 א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1* ;] 
  1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers. 
  2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, Matt.6:2, Luke.14:21 Acts.9:11 12:10 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).†
 (AS)

G4506.d:
ῥύομαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָצַל hi., also for גָּאַל, פָּלַט pi., etc. ;] 
to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), Matt.27:43, 2 Pet.2:7; id. before ἀπό, Matt.6:13, Luke.11:4 (Rec., R, mg.), 2 Tim.4:18; before ἐκ, Rom.7:24, 2 Cor.1:10, Col.1:13, 1 Thess.1:10, 2 Tim.3:11, 2 Pet.2:9; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, Rom.11:26. Passive: before ἀπό, Rom.15:31, 2 Thess.3:2; before ἐκ, Luke.1:74, 2 Tim.4:17.†
 (AS)

G4507.d:
ῥυπαρία, -ας, ἡ
 (ῥυπαρός) 
filthiness: metaphorically, of moral defile­ment, Jas.1:21.†
 (AS)

G4508.d:
ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν
 (ῥύπος), [in LXX: Zec.3:4-5, (3-4) (צוֹא)* ;] 
filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), Jas.2:2; metaphorically, of moral defilement, Rev.22:11.†
 (AS)

G4509.d:
ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Isa.4:4 (צוֹאָה), Job.14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;] 
dirt, filth: 1 Pet.3:21.†
 (AS)

G4510.d:
ῥυπόω, -ῶ 
 (ῥύπος), 
to make filthy: Rev.22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†
 (AS)

G4511.d:
ῥύσις, -εως, ἡ
 (ῥέω), [in LXX chiefly for זוֹב ;] 
a flowing, issue: τ. αἵματος, Mark.5:25, Luke.8:43-44.†
 (AS)

G4512.d: a fold  or pucker  in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G4513.d:
Roman, a Roman , (Polybius Historicus), etc.; adverb -κῶς, in Latin , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
 (ML)

G4517.d:
ῥώννυμι
 [in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 11:21 2Mac 11:28 2Mac 11:33 2Mac 11:1-38; 3Ma.6:1-41 * ;] 
to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Acts.15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.†
 (AS)

G4518.d:
σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי), 
 sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Matt.27:46, Mark.15:34 (Ps.22:2, Heb. עָזַב).†
  ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב), 
  zaphthanei: Matt.27:46 (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).†
 (AS)

G4519.d:
σαβαώθ  indecl., 
 [in LXX for צָבָא, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; see DB, iii, 137 f.) ;] 
Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (see DB, l.with): Rom.9:29 (LXX), Ja 54.†
 (AS)

G4520.d:
σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Exod.16:30, al.), 
a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaphorically, as in Mishna (Zorell, see word), Heb.4:9.†
 (AS)

G4522.d:
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם ;] 
a drag-net, seine: Matt.13:47.†
 SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), δίκτυον  (AS)

G4523.d:
Σαδδουκαῖος, -ου, ὁ
 (Heb. צָדוֹק, 2Ki.15:24, al.), 
a Sadducee (cf. Swete, Mk., 277): Matt.3:7 16:1, 6 16:11-12 22:23-34 Mark.12:18, Luke.20:27, Acts.4:1 5:17 23:6-8.†
 (AS)

G4524.d:
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος) 
 Sadoc, Zadok: Matt.1:14.†
 (AS)

G4525.d:
σαίνω 
  1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn. 
  2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1 Thess.3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).†
 (AS)

G4526.d:
σάκκος  also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ 
 (cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX), 
  1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Rev.6:12. 
  2. Anything made of sackcloth; 
  (a) a sack (Gen.42:25, al.); 
  (b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Matt.11:21, Luke.10:13, Rev.11:3.†
 (AS)

G4527.d:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח), 
 Sala, Shalah: Luke.3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luke.3:35.†
 (AS)

G4528.d:
Σαλαθιήλ, ὁ 
 indecl. (Heb. שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל), 
 Salathiel: Matt.1:12, Luke.3:27.†
 (AS)

G4529.d:
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνσς, ἡ 
 Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Acts.13:5.†
 (AS)

G4530.d:
Σαλείμ, τό indecl., 
 Salim: John.3:23 (see Westc., in l; DB, iii, 354).†
 (AS)

G4532.d:
Σαλήμ, ἡ (Heb. שָׁלֵם Gen.14:18), 
 Salem: Heb.7:1-2 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4533.d:
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן), 
 Salmon: Matt.1:4-5, Luke.3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†
 (AS)

G4534.d:
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ 
 Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Acts.27:7.†
 (AS)

G4535.d:
σάλος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;] 
in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Luke.21:25.†
 (AS)

G4536.d:
σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;] 
a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: 1 Cor.14:8, Heb.12:19, Rev.1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Matt.24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, 1 Thess.4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., 1 Cor.15:52.†
 (AS)

G4537.d:
σαλπίζω 
 [in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;] 
to sound a trumpet: Rev.8:6 ff. Rev.9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaphorically, Matt.6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: 1 Cor.15:52.†
 (AS)

G4538.d:
σαλπιστής
 (so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ, 
a trumpeter: Rev.18:22.†
 (AS)

G4541.d:
Σαμαρείτης
 (-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό, 
a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): Matt.10:5, Luke.9:52 10:33 17:16, John.4:9, 39-40, Acts.8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, John.8:48.†
 (AS)

G4542.d:
Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, see supr.), -ιδος, ἡ 
  1. in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria. 
  2. a Samaritan woman: John.4:9.†
 (AS)

G4543.d:
Σαμοθρᾴκη
 (-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ 
Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: Acts.16:11.†
 (AS)

G4544.d:
Σάμος, -ου, ἡ 
 Samos, an island in the Ægean: Acts.20:15.†
 (AS)

G4545.d:
Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl. 
 (in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל), 
Samuel (1Ki.1:20, al.): Acts.3:24 13:20, Heb.11:32.†
 (AS)

G4546.d:
Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן), 
 Samson (Jdg.13:1-25 ff.): Heb.11:32.†
 (AS)

G4547.d:
σανδάλιον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Jos.9:5, Isa.20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, which see), Jdth.10:4 16:9 * ;] 
a sandal: Mark.6:9, Acts.12:8.†
 (AS)

G4548.d:
σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Sng.8:9, Eze.27:5 (לוּחַ) * ;] 
a board, plank: Acts.27:44 
 (AS)

G4550.d:
σαπρός, -ά -όν 
 [in Sm.: Lev.27:14, 33 * ;] 
rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός), Matt.7:17-18 12:33 Luke.6:43; of fish, Matt.13:48. 
 Metaphorical, in moral sense: λόγος σ., Eph.4:29. "In Hellenistic . . . it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.†
 (AS)

G4551.d:
Σαπφείρα, -ης (see B1., § 3, 4), ἡ 
 (Aram. שַׁפִּירָא) 
Sapphia: Acts.5:1.†
 (AS)

G4552.d:
σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ 
 [in LXX for סַפִּיר ;] 
sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Rev.21:19.†
 (AS)

G4553.d:
σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ 
  1. a plaited rope (Æsch.). 
  2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: 2 Cor.11:33.†
 (AS)

G4554.d:
Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ 
 Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Rev.1:11 3:1, 4 
 (AS)

G4555.d:
σάρδινος, -ου, ὁ 
 = σάρδιον (which see), Rev.4:3, Rec.†
 (AS)

G4556.d:
σάρδιον, -ον, τ 
 [in LXX for אֹדֶם, Exod.28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;] 
the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Rev.4:3 21:20.†
 (AS)

G4557.d:
σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ 
 (σάρδιον, ὄνυξ), 
sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Rev.21:20.†
 (AS)

G4558.d:
Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת), 
 Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Luke.4:26.†
 (AS)

G4559.d:
σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (σάρξ) 
 (seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7) 
= Lat. carnalis, i.e. 
  (a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Rom.15:27, 1 Cor.9:11; 
  (b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): 1 Cor.3:3, 2 Cor.1:12 10:4, 1 Pet.2:11.†
 SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ LXXi, LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Rom.7:14  (AS)

G4560.d:
σάρκινος, -η, -ον
 (σάρξ), [in LXX: 2Ch.32:8, Eze.11:19 36:26 (בָּשָׂר), Est.4:17, Pro.24:23 (Pro.29:27) * ;] 
= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Rom.7:14, 1 Cor.3:1, 2 Cor.3:3, Heb.7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except 2 Cor.3:3, but the evidence is decisive against it.)†
 SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v  (AS)

G4562.d:
Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג), 
 Serug: Luke.3:35.† 
 (AS)

G4563.d:
σαρόω, -ῶ 
 late form of σαίρω, 
 to sweep: with accusative, Luke.15:8; pass., Matt.12:44, Luke.11:25.†
 (AS)

G4564.d:
Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, Gen.17:15), 
 Sarah: Rom.4:19 9:9, Heb.11:11, 1 Pet.3:6.†
 (AS)

G4565.d:
Σάρων, -ωνος (accusative -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן), 
 the plain of Sharon: Acts.9:35.†
 (AS)

G4566.d:
Satan , i. e. an adversary, enemy : name for the Devil , (New Testament) 
Hebr. word. (ML)

G4567.d:
Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ
 (so also Sir 21:30, but in 3Ki.11:14, σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό, 
Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. with): Matt.4:10 12:26, Mark.1:13 3:23, 26 4:15 Luke.10:18 11:18 13:16 22:3, 31, John.13:27, Acts.5:3 26:18, Rom.16:20, 1 Cor.5:5 7:5, 2 Cor.2:11 11:14, 1 Thess.2:18, 2 Thess.2:9, 1 Tim.1:20 5:15, Rev.2:9, 13 2:24 3:9 12:9 20:2, 7; addressed in person of Peter, Matt.16:23 Mark.8:33; ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, 2 Cor.12:7.†
 (AS)

G4568.d:
σάτον, -ου, τό
 (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Hag.2:17 (16)* ;] 
a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Matt.13:33, Luke.13:21.†
 (AS)

G4569.d:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see), 
 Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: Acts.7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9.†
 (AS)

G4570.d:
σβέννυμι 
 [in LXX chiefly for כָּבָה ;] 
of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, Matt.12:20, Eph.6:16, Heb.11:34; pass., Matt.25:8, Mark.9:48, [44, 46]. Metaphorical (cf. Sng.8:7, 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, 1 Thess.5:19.†
 ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, 1 Thess.5:19 T (see WH, Notes, 148).†
 (AS)

G4571.d:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό, 
 determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).  
  1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); 
  (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luke.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, John.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, John.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, John.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mark.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mark.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Matt.3:4, Mark.6:17, John.16:27, 1 Thess.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luke.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word); 
  (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Matt.1:21, 12:50, Luke.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Matt.8:24, Mark.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Matt.14:2, Mark.14:15, 44, Luke.1:22, 2:28, al.
  2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Matt.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Matt.9:18, Mark.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mark.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Matt.4:23, Acts.8:5, 2 Cor.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1 Thess.2:19, Titus.3:5, Heb.2:4.
  3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Matt.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Phil.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Acts.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Acts.14:1, Luke.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Matt.22:34, Acts.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1 Cor.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1 Cor.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mark.14:39; μέτρος, Phil.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1 Cor.12:4.
 (AS)

G4572.d:
σεαυτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ
 (in NT not contracted, σαυτοῦ, as in Att..), 
 reflex. prop. of 2nd of person(s) sing., used only in genitive, dative and accusative  
(of, to) thyself: Matt.4:6, John.8:13, 1 Tim.4:16, al. (In Hellenistic, the pl. is ἑαυτῶν (which see), not ὑμῶν αὐτῶν as in Attic, see Bl., § 13, 1.) †
 (AS)

G4573.d:
σεβάζομαι
 (σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: Hos.10:5 * ;] 
  1. to fear (Hom). 
  2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Rom.1:25 
 (AS)

G4574.d:
σέβασμα, -τος, τό
 (σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;] 
an object of worship: Acts.17:23, 2 Thess.2:4.†
 (AS)

G4576.d:
σέβω 
 [in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, Jos.4:24, al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. 4Ma.5:24 ;] 
to worship: with accusative of person(s), Matt.15:9, Mark.7:7, Acts.18:13 19:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, Acts.16:14 18:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, Acts.13:43, 50 17:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†
 (AS)

G4577.d:
σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Jdg.16:13-14, 19 (מַחְלָפָה), Pro.5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;] 
  1. (a) a cord; 
  (b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.with): σειραὶ ζόφου, 2 Pet.2:4, Rec., R, mg. (see: σειρός). 
  2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. with).†
 (AS)

G4578.d:
σεισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ ;] 
a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: Matt.8:24; esp. an earthquake: Matt.24:7 27:54 28:2, Mark.13:8, Luke.21:11, Acts.16:26, Rev.6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18.†
 (AS)

G4579.d:
σείω 
 [in LXX chiefly for רָעַשׁ ;] 
to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, Heb.12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Matt.27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Rev.6:13. Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Matt.21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†
 (AS)

G4581.d:
Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια), 
 Seleucia, a city of Syria: Acts.13:4.† 
 (AS)

G4582.d:
σελήνη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ (Gen.37:9, al.), also for לְבָנָה; (Sng.6:9(10), ?Isa.24:23 30:26) ;] 
the moon: Matt.24:29, Mark.13:24, Luke.21:25, Acts.2:20" (LXX), 1 Cor.15:41, Rev.6:12 8:12 12:1 21:23.†
 (AS)

G4583.d:
σεληνιάζω
 (σελήνη), 
 act, in Manetho (Caren., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι, 
 to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Matt.4:24 17:15.†
 (AS)

G4584.d:
Σεμεείν (Rec. Σεμεΐ), ὁ, indecl., 
 Semein: Luke.3:26.†
 (AS)

G4585.d:
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;] 
fine wheaten flour: Rev.18:13.†
 (AS)

G4586.d:
σεμνός, -ή, -όν 
 (σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pro.6:8 8:6 15:26, 2Ma.6:11 2Mac 6:28 2Mac 8:15, 4Ma.5:36 4Mac 7:15 4Mac 17:5 * ;] 
  1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings. 
  2. grave, serious; of persons: 1 Tim.3:8 3:11, Titus.2:2; of things: Phil.4:8 (see Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†
 (AS)

G4587.d:
σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ
 (σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;] 
gravity: 1 Tim.2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Titus.2:7.† 
 (AS)

G4588.d:
Σέργιος, -ου, ὁ 
 Sergius, surnamed Paulus: Acts.13:7.†
 (AS)

G4589.d:
Σήθ, ὁ (Heb. שֵׁת), 
 indecl., 
 Seth (Gen.4:25): Luke.3:38.†
 (AS)

G4590.d:
Σήμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֵׁם), 
 Shem: Luke.3:36.†
 (AS)

G4591.d:
σημαίνω
 (σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע, etc. ;] 
to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), Acts.25:27, Rev.1:1 (cf. MM, xxii); with accusative and inf., Acts.11:28; before quæst. indir., John.12:33 18:32 21:19.†
 (AS)

G4593.d:
σημειόω, -ῶ
 (σημεῖον), [in LXX: Ps.4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;] 
to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2 Thess.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).†
 (AS)

G4594.d:
σήμερον (Att.. τήμερον), 
 adv., [in LXX for יוֹם ;] 
to-day: Matt.6:11, Luke.4:21, Acts.4:9, al.; opposite to αὔριον, Matt.6:30, Luke.12:28, Jas.4:13; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, Heb.13:8; ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, Acts.20:20; ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, Rom.11:8, 2 Cor.3:14; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), Matt.11:23 27:8; as subst., τὸ σ., Heb.3:13; id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμὶραν, σ., Heb.4:7 R, mg., (see Westc., in l) 
 (AS)

G4595.d:
σήπω 
 [in LXX; Ps.38:5 (מָקַק ni.), Job.33:21 (כָּלָה) Job.40:7, Sir.14:19, al. ;] 
to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (see M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, Jas.5:2.†
 (AS)

G4596.d:
σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν 
 (οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk), 
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Rev.18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†
 (AS)

G4597.d:
σής  σητός (late genitive for cl. σεός), ὁ, 
 [in LXX: Job.4:19, Isa.50:9 (עָשׁ), Isa.51:8 (סָס), al. ;] 
a moth, clothes moth: Matt.6:19-20, Luke.12:33.†
 (AS)

G4598.d:
σητό-βρωτος, -ον
 (οής, βιβρώσκω), [in LXX: Job.13:28 (אָכַל עָשׁ) * ;] 
moth-eaten: Jas.5:2.†
 (AS)

G4599.d:
σθενόω, -ῶ
 (σθένος, strength), 
to strengthen: with accusative, 1 Pet.5:10 (Hesych.).†
 (AS)

G4600.d:
σιαγών, -όνος, ἡ 
 [in LXX for לְחִי ;] 
the jawbone, jaw, cheek: Matt.5:39, Luke.6:29 (cf. MM, xxii).†
 (AS)

G4601.d:
σιγάω, -ῶ
 (σιγή), [in LXX for חָרַשׁ, חָשָׁה, etc. ;] 
  1. intrans.,  to be silent, keep silence: Luke.9:36 18:39 20:26, Acts.12:17 15:12-13, 1 Cor.14:28 14:30 14:34. 
  2. Trans., to keep secret; pass., to be kept secret: Rom.16:25.†
 SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιωπάω  (AS)

G4602.d:
σιγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Wis.18:14, 3Ma.3:23 * ;] 
silence: Acts.21:40, Rev.8:1.†
 (AS)

G4603.d:
σιδήρεος, -α, -ον (-οῦς, -ᾶ -οῦν)
 (σίδηρος), [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;] 
of iron: Acts.12:10, Rev.2:27 9:9 12:5 19:15.†
 (AS)

G4604.d:
σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;] 
iron: Rev.18:12.†
 (AS)

G4605.d:
Σιδών, -ῶnος, ἡ (Heb. צִידוֹן), 
 Sidon, a maritime city of Phœnicia: Matt.11:21-22 15:21, Mark.3:8 7:24, 31, Luke.6:17 10:13-14, Acts.27:3.†
 (AS)

G4607.d:
σικάριος, -ου, ὁ
 (Lat.; sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii), 
a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Acts.21:38.†
 (AS)

G4608.d:
σίκερα, τό indecl. 
 (Aram. שִׁכְרָא), [in LXX for שֵׁכָר (also rendered μέθυσμα, Jdg.13:4, Mic.2:11), Lev.10:9, al. ;] 
fermented liquor, strong drink: Luke.1:15.†
 (AS)

G4609.d:
Σίλας, -α (accusative to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; see Dalman, Gr., 157.5), 
 Silas (called also Σιλουανός, which see): Acts.15:22, 27 15:32, 34 15:40 16:19, 25 16:29 17:4, 10 17:14-15 18:5 †
 (AS)

G4610.d:
Σιλουανός
 (in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form frequently in π.), -οῦ, ὁ, 
Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: 2 Cor.1:19, 1 Thess.1:1, 2 Thess.1:1, 1 Pet.5:12.†
 (AS)

G4611.d:
Σιλωάμ (indecl., but in FlJ, genitive, ᾶ, B.J., ii, 16, 2), ὁ (Heb. שִׁלֹחַ), 
 Siloam (see DB, iii, 515 f.): Luke.13:4, John.9:7, 11.†
 (AS)

G4612.d:
σιμικίνθιον (also written σημι-), -ου, τό (Lat. semicinctium), 
 a work­man's apron: Acts.19:12.†
 (AS)

G4613.d:
Σίμων, -ωνος, ὁ 
 a Greek name (transliterated סִימוֺן in Heb.) used as a substitute for Συμεών (which see), Simon 
  1. Simon Peter: Matt.17:25, Mark.1:29, al. 
  2. Simon the Zealot (see: ζηλωτής, Καναναῖος): Matt.10:4, Mark.3:18, Luke.6:15, Acts.1:13. 
  3. One of the Brethren of our Lord (see: ἀδελψός): Matt.13:55, Mark.6:3. 
  4. The father of Judas Iscariot, himself surnamed Ἰσκαριώτης (which see): John.6:71 12:4 (Rec.) 13:2,26 
  5. Simon the Cyrenian: Matt.27:32, Mark.15:21, Luke.23:26. 
  6. Simon the Pharisee: Luke.7:40, 43-44. 
  7. Simon of Bethany, surnamed ὁ λεπρός: Matt.26:6, Mark.14:3. 
  8. Simon Magus, a Samaritan sorcerer: Acts.8:9, 13 8:18, 24. 
  9. Simon the tanner, of Joppa: Acts.9:43 10:6, 17 10:32 
 (AS)

G4614.d:
Σινά
 (-ᾶ, Rec.), 
indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό 
 (Heb. סִינַי), 
Sinai (Exod.19:11, al.): Acts.7:30, 38, Gal.4:24-25†
 (AS)

G4615.d:
σίναπι, -εως, τό
 (prob. Egyptian), = Attic τὸ νᾶπυ 
mustard: Matt.13:31 17:20, Mark.4:31, Luke.13:19 17:6.†
 (AS)

G4617.d:
σινιάω
 (σίνιον, a sieve), = σήθω, 
to sift, winnow: figuratively, Luke.22:31.†
 (AS)

G4618.d:
σιτευτός, -ή, -όν
 (σιτεύω, to feed, fatten), [in LXX: 3Ki.4:23 (אָבַס), etc. ;] 
fattened: Luke.15:23, 27 15:30.†
 (AS)

G4619.d:
σιτιστός, -ή, -όν
 (σιτίζω, to fatten) [in Sm.: Ps.22:13, Jer.46:21 * ;] 
= σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: Matt.22:4.†
 (AS)

G4620.d:
σιτομέτριον, -ου, τό
 (σιτομετρέω, Gen.47:12, 14 *, = Attic τὸν σῖτον μετρέω), 
a measured portion of food: Luke.12:42 (for exx. in π., see Deiss., BS, 158; LAE, 103.1).†
 (AS)

G4621.d:
σῖτος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for דָּגָן ;] 
wheat, corn: Matt.3:12 13:25, 29-30 Mark.4:28, Luke.3:17 12:18 16:7 22:32, John.12:24, Acts.27:38, 1 Cor.15:37, Rev.6:6 18:13.†
 σιτίοι, -ου, τό 
 (dimin. of σῖτος), [in LXX: Pro.30:22 (לֶחֶם)* ;] 
  1. corn, grain: Acts.7:12 (but see 131., § 9, 1). 
  2. Mostly in pl., σιτία, bread, food, provisions (LXX, l.with, Hdt., al.).†
 (AS)

G4623.d:
σιωπάω, -ῶ
 (σιωπή, silence) [in LXX for חָשָׁה, חָרַשׁ hi., etc. ;] 
to be silent or still, keep silence: Matt.20:31 26:63, Mark.3:4 9:34 10:48 14:61, Luke.19:4, Acts.18:9; of one dumb, Luke.1:20 (cf. 4Ma.10:18); addressed rhetorically to the sea, σιώπα, Mark.4:39.†
 SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιγάω (which see)  (AS)

G4624.d:
σκανδαλίζω
 (σκάνδαλον), [in LXX: Dan LXX 11:41 (כָּשַׁל ni.), Sir.9:5 (Sir.35:15 32:15) (יָקֹשׁ ho.) Sir.23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Psa Sol Ps.16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)* ;] 
prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaphorically of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: with accusative of person(s), Matt.5:29-30 17:27 18:6, 8-9 Mark.9:42-43, 45 9:47 Luke.17:2, John.6:61, 1 Cor.8:13. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: Matt.11:6 13:21, 57 15:12 24:10 26:31, 33, Mark.4:17 6:3 14:27, 29, Luke.7:23, John.16:1, Rom.14:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), 2 Cor.11:29,†
 (AS)

G4626.d:
σκάπτω 
 [in LXX: Isa.5:6 (עֲדַר ni.)* ;] 
to dig: Luke.6:48 13:8 16:3.†
 (AS)

G4627.d:
σκάφη, -ης, ἡ
 (σκάπτω), [in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, TH Bel 1:33 * ;] 
anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Acts.27:16, 30 27:32.†
 (AS)

G4628.d:
σκέλος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX for רֶגֶל, etc. ;] 
the leg from the hip downwards: ?John.19:3-33 †
 (AS)

G4629.d:
σκέπασμα, -τος, τό
 (σκεπάζω, to cover), 
a covering, esp. clothing: 1 Tim.6:8.†
 (AS)

G4631.d:
σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: 3Ma.5:45 R * ;] 
equipment, tackle: Acts.27:19.†
 (AS)

G4632.d:
σκεῦος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;] 
a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, see MM, xxii): Mark.11:16, Luke.8:16, John.19:29, Acts.10:11, 16 11:5, Rom.9:21, Rev.18:12; pl., 2 Tim.2:20, Rev.2:27; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, Heb.9:21; pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, Matt.12:29, Mark.3:27, Luke.17:31; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., Acts.27:17. Metaphorical, of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, Acts.9:15; ὀργῆς, Rom.9:22; ἐλέους, Rom.9:23; σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. Rom.9:21), 2 Tim.2:21; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., 1 Pet.3:7; so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., 1 Thess.4:4 (but see infr.); of the body, 2 Cor.4:7; so perh. 1 Thess.4:4 (but see supr., and see: κτάομαι).†
  κτάομαι, -ῶμαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָנָה ;] 
in pres., impf., fut. and aor., to procure for oneself, get, gain, acquire (the pf. and plpf., to have acquired, hence to possess, do not occur in NT): with accusative of thing(s), Matt.10:9, Luke.18:12, Acts.8:20; with genitive pret., Acts.22:28; ἐκ with genitive pret., Acts.1:18; τ,ψυχὰς ὑμῶν (MM, xvi), Luke.21:19; τ. ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι, 1 Thess.4:4 (where if σ. = body, κ. must = pf., κέκτημαι; see MM, xvi; M, Th., in l; Field, Notes, 72 f. But σ. is most frequently taken as = wife; see Thayer, see word; Lft., Notes, 53 ff.; ICC, in l).†
 (AS)

G4633.d:
σκηνή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל, also for מִשְׁכָּן, סֻכָּה, etc. ;] 
a tent, booth, tabernacle: Matt.17:4, Mark.9:5, Luke.9:33, Heb.11:9; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., Luke.16:9; of the Mosaic tabernacle, Heb.8:5 9:2-3, 6 9:8, 21; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, Acts.7:44; of its heavenly prototype, Heb.8:2 9:11, Rev.13:6 15:5 21:3; of the temple, Heb.13:10; ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, Acts.7:43 (LXX); metaphorically, ἡ σ. Δαυείδ Acts.15:16 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4634.d:
σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ
 (σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכָּה, Deu.16:16 31:10, Zec.14:16, 18-19; I Est.5:51, 1Ma.10:21, 2Ma.1:9 2Mac 1:18 * ;] 
prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, Lev.23:34, al.; see Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: John.7:2.†
 (AS)

G4635.d:
σκηνοποιός, -όν
 (σκηνή, ποιέω), 
making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Acts.18:3.†
 (AS)

G4636.d:
σκῆνος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX: Wis.9:15 * ;] 
= σκηνή, 
 a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: 2 Cor.5:1 5:4.†
 (AS)

G4637.d:
σκηνόω, -ῶ
 (σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַן ;] 
to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, see MM, Exp., xxii): before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Rev.7:15; before ἐν, with dative of person(s), John.1:14; id. with dative loc., Rev.12:12 13:6; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Rev.21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).†
 (AS)

G4638.d:
σκήνωμα, -τος, τό
 (σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;] 
a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Ps.132:5, al.), Acts.7:46. Metaphorical, of the body: 2 Pet.1:13-14.†
 (AS)

G4639.d:
σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for צֵל, 4Ki.20:9 ff., Ps.57:1, al.; but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, Job.3:5, Ps.3:4, Isa.9:2 (1) (see ICC, in l), al. ;] 
  1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: Mark.4:32, Acts.5:15; metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, Matt.4:16, Luke.1:79" (LXX) . 
  2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., Heb.8:5; opposite to σῶμα, Col.2:17; opposite to εἰκών, Heb.10:1.†
 (AS)

G4640.d:
σκιρτάω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Gen.25:22 (רָצַץ hithpo.), Ps.114:4, 6 (רָקַד), etc. ;] 
to leap: Luke.1:41, 44 6:23.†
 (AS)

G4641.d:
σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ
 (σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: Deu.10:16, Jer.4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Sir.16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, Sir.3:26-27) * ;] 
hardness of heart: Matt.19:8, Mark.10:5 16:14.†
 (AS)

G4643.d:
σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ
 (σκληρός), [in LXX: Deu.9:27 (קְשִׁי), etc. ;] 
hardness; metaphorically, of stubbornness: Rom.2:5.†
 (AS)

G4644.d:
σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον
 (σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: Exod.33:3, 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;] 
stiff-necked: metaphorically, Acts.7:51.†
 (AS)

G4645.d:
σκληρύνω
 (σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה hi., also for חָזַק ;] 
to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), Rom.9:18; T. καρδίας (Ps.95:8), Heb.3:8, 15 4:7. Pass., to become hardened: Acts.19:9, Heb.3:13.†
 (AS)

G4646.d:
σκολιός, -ά, -όν 
 [in LXX: Deu.32:5 (עִקֵּשׁ), Pro.28:18 (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דֶּרֶךְ עָקַשׁ), Isa.40:4 (עָקֹב), etc. ;] 
curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): Luke.3:5 (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust: Acts.2:40, Phil.2:15, 1 Pet.2:18.†
 (AS)

G4647.d:
σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Num.33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Hos.2:6 (8) (סִיר), Eze.28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Sir.43:19 * ;] 
anything pointed, esp. 
  1. in cl., a stake 
  2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, 2 Cor.12:7  (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†
 (AS)

G4648.d:
ακοπέω, -ῶ
 (σκοπός), [in LXX: Est.8:13, 2Ma.4:5 * ;] 
to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), 2 Cor.4:13, Phil.2:4; with accusative of person(s), Rom.16:17, Phil.3:17; before μή, Luke.11:35; σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), Gal.6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).†
 SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω  (AS)

G4649.d:
σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה ;] 
  1. a watcher, watchman (Eze.3:17, al.). 
  2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wis.5:12, 21, al.). Metaphorical, of an aim or object: Phil.3:14.†
 (AS)

G4650.d:
σκορπίζω 
 [in LXX for פּוּץ hi., etc. ;] 
in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (see MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, John.10:12; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, Matt.12:30, Luke.11:23; pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., John.16:32; of one who dispenses blessings, 2 Cor.9:9 (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).†
 (AS)

G4651.d:
σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX for עַקְרָב ;] 
a scorpion: Luke.10:19 11:12, Rev.9:3, 5 9:10 †
 (AS)

G4652.d:
σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν
 (σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;] 
dark: opposite to φωτεινός, Matt.6:23, Luke.11:34, 36.†
 (AS)

G4653.d:
σκοτία, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Job.28:3 (אֹפֶל), Mic.3:6 (חָשַׁךְ), Isa.16:3 * ;] 
in late writers = σκότος, 
 darkness: John.6:17 20:1. Metaphorical, 
  (a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): Matt.10:27, Luke.12:3; 
  (b) of spiritual darkness: Matt.4:16, John.1:5 8:12 12:35, 40, 1 John.1:5 Jn 2:8-9 Jn 2:11.†
 (AS)

G4654.d:
σκοτίζω
 (σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ ;] 
to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Matt.24:29, Mark.13:24, Luke.23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Rev.8:12. Metaphorical, of the mind, Rom.1:21 11:10" (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).†
 (AS)

G4655.d:
σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf.σ., τό), 
 darkness: Heb.12:18, Rec.†
 (AS)

G4656.d:
σκοτόω, -ῶ
 (σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר ;] 
to darken: Rev.9:2 16:10. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., Eph.4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).†
 (AS)

G4657.d:
σκύβαλον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX: Sir.27:4 * ;] 
refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Phil.3:8.†
 (AS)

G4658.d:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ 
 Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col.3:11.†
 (AS)

G4659.d:
σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν) 
 (σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), [in LXX: Gen.40:7 (רַע), etc. ;] 
of a gloomy countenance: Matt.6:16, Luke.24:17.†
 (AS)

G4660.d:
σκύλλω 
  1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.). 
  2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), Mark.5:35, Luke.8:49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Matt.9:36; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Luke.7:6 (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).†
 (AS)

G4661.d:
σκῦλον
 (Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;] 
mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Luke.11:22.†
 (AS)

G4662.d:
σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον
 (σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω), 
eaten of worms: Acts.12:23 (cf. 2Ma.9:9, and see MM, xxiii) †
 (AS)

G4663.d:
σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;] 
a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, Mark.9:48 (LXX, Isa.66:24; cf. Sir.7:17, Jdth.16:17).†
 (AS)

G4664.d:
σμαράγδινος
 (σμάραγδος, which see), 
  1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11). 
  2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Rev.4:3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).†
 (AS)

G4665.d:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ
 (and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Exod.28:9 (שֹׁהַם) Exod.36:17 (Exod.39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Eze.28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;] 
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Rev.21:19.†
 (AS)

G4666.d:
σμύρνα
 (in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מֹר ;] 
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Matt.2:11, John.19:39.†
 (AS)

G4667.d:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ 
 Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.†
 Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, 
 Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
 (AS)

G4668.d:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ 
 Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.†
 Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, 
 Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
 (AS)

G4669.d:
σμυρνίζω
 (σιύρνα), 
  1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79). 
  2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mark.15:23.†
 (AS)

G4670.d:
Σόδομα, -ων, τά (Heb. סְדֹם), 
 Sodom (Gen.13:10, 12, al.): Matt.10:15 11:23-24 Luke.10:12 17:29, Rom.9:29" (LXX), 2 Pet.2:6, Ju 7, Rev.11:8.†
 (AS)

G4671.d:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό, 
 determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).  
  1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); 
  (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luke.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, John.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, John.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, John.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mark.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mark.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Matt.3:4, Mark.6:17, John.16:27, 1 Thess.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luke.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word); 
  (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Matt.1:21, 12:50, Luke.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Matt.8:24, Mark.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Matt.14:2, Mark.14:15, 44, Luke.1:22, 2:28, al.
  2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Matt.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Matt.9:18, Mark.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mark.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Matt.4:23, Acts.8:5, 2 Cor.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1 Thess.2:19, Titus.3:5, Heb.2:4.
  3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Matt.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Phil.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Acts.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Acts.14:1, Luke.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Matt.22:34, Acts.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1 Cor.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1 Cor.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mark.14:39; μέτρος, Phil.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1 Cor.12:4.
 (AS)

G4672.d:
Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Acts.3:11 5:12; in Acts.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), 
 Solomon: Matt.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luke.11:31 12:27, John.10:23, Acts.3:11 5:12 7:47.†
 (AS)

G4673.d:
σορός, -οῦ, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Gen.50:26 (אָרוֹן), Job.21:32 A * ;] 
  (a) a cinerary urn (Hom.); 
  (b) a coffin (Hdt., i, 68, 3, a1.): Luke.7:14.†
 (AS)

G4674.d:
σός, -ή, -όν 
 possess. prop. of second of person(s), 
 thy, thine: Matt.7:3, al.; as subst., οἱ σοί, thy kinsfolk, friends, Mark.5:19; τὸ σόν, what is thine, Matt.20:14 25:25; τὰ σά, thy goods, Luke.6:30 
 (AS)

G4675.d:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό, 
 determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).  
  1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); 
  (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luke.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, John.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, John.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, John.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mark.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mark.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Matt.3:4, Mark.6:17, John.16:27, 1 Thess.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luke.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word); 
  (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), Matt.1:21, 12:50, Luke.6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Matt.8:24, Mark.4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), Matt.14:2, Mark.14:15, 44, Luke.1:22, 2:28, al.
  2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, Matt.7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., Matt.9:18, Mark.13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), Mark.7:25, Rev.3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Matt.4:23, Acts.8:5, 2 Cor.2:13, al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Rom.11:11, 1 Thess.2:19, Titus.3:5, Heb.2:4.
  3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: Heb.1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Matt.5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Rom.12:16, 15:5, Phil.2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Acts.15:27, Rom.2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), Acts.14:1, Luke.6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), Matt.22:34, Acts.1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., 1 Cor.11:5, 12:11; with dative (cl.), 1 Cor.11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mark.14:39; μέτρος, Phil.1:30; πνεῦμα, 1 Cor.12:4.
 (AS)

G4676.d:
σουδάριον, -ου, τό(Lat.), 
 handkerchief, kerchief: Luke.19:20, Acts.19:12; used as a head covering for the dead, John.11:44 20:7 (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).†
 (AS)

G4677.d:
Σουσάννα, -ης
 (cf. Dan LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.) 
Susanna: Luke.8:3.†
 (AS)

G4679.d:
σοφίζω
 (σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] 
to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), 2 Tim.3:15 (cf. Ps.19:8 (Ps.119:98). As depon., -ομαι; 
  (a) intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 (3Ki.5:11), Ecc.2:15, and frequently in Sir.7:5, al.); 
  (b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., 2 Pet.1:16 
 (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).†
 (AS)

G4680.d:
σοφός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] 
skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: Rom.16:19, 1 Cor.3:10; of the learned, Rom.1:14, 22, 1 Cor.1:19-20 1:26-27 3:18-20; of Jewish teachers, Matt.11:25, Luke.10:21; Christian, Matt.23:34; of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, 1 Cor.6:5, Eph.5:15, Jas.3:13; of God, Rom.16:27; compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, 1 Cor.1:25.†
 SYN.: συνετός, φρόνιμος (see: σοφία, SYN.)  (AS)

G4681.d:
Σπανία, -ας, ἡ
 (= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (1Ma.8:3) or Σ. as here), 
Spain: Rom.15:24, 28.†
 (AS)

G4682.d:
σπαράσσω 
 [in LXX: 2Ki.22:8 B (גָּעַשׁ hith.), John.4:19 (הָמָה) Dan LXX 8:7 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), 3Ma.4:6 * ;] 
  1. to tear, rend, mangle. 
  2. to convulse: Mark.1:26 (see Swete, in l) Mark.9:26, Luke.9:39 
 (cf. συν-σπαράσσω).†
 (AS)

G4683.d:
σπαργανόω, -ῶ
 (σπάργανον, a swathing-band) [in LXX: Job.38:9, Eze.16:4 (חָתַל pu.)* ;] 
to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: Luke.2:7, 12 (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).†
 (AS)

G4684.d:
σπαταλάω, -ῶ
 (σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Sir.27:13 *), [in LXX: Eze.16:49 (שָׁקַט hi.), Sir.21:15 * ;] 
to live riotously: 1 Tim.5:6, Jas.5:5 (Polyb.).†
 SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (see Tr., Syn., § liv)  (AS)

G4685.d:
σπάω 
 [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַף, ;] 
in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157), 
 to draw: μάχαιραν, Mark.14:47, Acts.16:27,†
 (AS)

G4686.d:
σπείρα, -ης
 (on this form of genitive, see M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186), [in LXX: Jdth.14:11, 2Ma.8:23 2Mac 12:20 2Mac 12:22 * ;] 
  1. (= Lat. spira) anything wound or rolled up, a coil. 
  2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (see Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): Matt.27:27, Mark.15:16, John.18:3, 12, Acts.10:1 21:31 27:1.†
 (AS)

G4687.d:
σπείρω
 [in LXX chiefly for זָרַע ;] 
to sow (seed): absol., Matt.6:26 13:3-4, 18 25:24, 26, Mark.4:3-4, Luke.8:5 12:24, John.4:36, 2 Cor.9:10; with accusative of thing(s), Matt.13:24, 27 13:37, 39, Mark.4:32, Luke.8:5, 1 Cor.15:36-37; before εἰς, Matt.13:22, Mark.4:18; ἐν, Matt.13:24, 31; ἐπί, with genitive, Mark.4:31; ἐπί, with accusative, Matt.13:20, 23, Mark.4:16, 20; παρά, with accusative, Matt.13:19. Metaphorical: 1 Cor.9:11 15:42-44, Gal.6:7-8, Jas.3:18; in proverbial sayings, Matt.25:24, 26, Luke.19:21-22, John.4:37, 2 Cor.9:6, Gal.6:7; in interpretation of parables, Matt.13:19-23 Mark.4:14-20 †
 (AS)

G4688.d:
σπεκουλάτωρ, -ορος (Rec. -ωρος), ὁ (Lat. speculator), 
  1. prop., a spy or scout. 
  2. An executioner: Mark.6:27 (see Swete, in l).†
 (AS)

G4689.d:
σπένδω 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָסַךְ hi. ;] 
to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., figuratively, σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Phil.2:17 (see Lft., in l), 2 Tim.4:6 (for exx. from π., see Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†
 (AS)

G4692.d:
σπεύδω 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi., also for בָּהַל pi., hi., etc. ;] 
  1. most frequently intrans., to hasten: with inf. (as frequently in cl.), Acts.20:16; ptcp. with indic., Luke.2:16; with imperat., Luke.19:5-6; σπεῦσον κ. ἔξελθε, Acts.22:18 
  2. Trans., with accusative; 
  (a) to hasten, urge on, accelerate (as Hom., Od., xix, 137; Eur., Med., 152; Sir.33:8 (Sir.36:8): 2 Pet.3:12, R, mg. (cf. Mayor and ICC, in l, but see infr.); 
  (b) to desire eagerly (find., Pyth., iii, 110; Eur., Suppl., 161; Isa 165): 2Pe, l.with, R, txt. (but see supr.).†
 (AS)

G4693.d:
σπήλαιον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה ;] 
a cave, cavern: John.11:38, Heb.11:38, Heb.6:15; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν (John.7:11), Matt.21:13, Mark.11:17, Luke.19:46.†
 (AS)

G4694.d:
σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ
 (on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41), 
  1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.). 
  2. In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).†
 (AS)

G4695.d:
σπιλόω 
 [in LXX: Wis.15:4 * ;] 
to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, Jas.3:6, Ju 23.†
 (AS)

G4696.d:
σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ 
  1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.). 
  2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (see Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaphorically, 
  (a) of moral blemish: Eph.5:27 
  (b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l): 2 Pet.2:13.†
 (AS)

G4697.d:
σπλαγχνίζομαι
 (σπλάγχνον), [in LXX (act., -ίζω): Pro.17:5 A, 2Ma.6:8 (= -εύω) * ;] 
to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., Luke.10:33 15:20; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., Matt.18:27 20:34, Mark.1:41; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), Matt.14:14, Luke.7:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Matt.15:32, Mark.6:34 8:2 9:22; ωερί, Matt.9:36. (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: 1Ki.23:21, Eze.24:21, Test. Zeb., 4:6-7; see Thayer, see word; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on Phil.1:8, in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) †
 (AS)

G4698.d:
σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, 
 [in LXX: Pro.12:10 (רַחַם, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, Ps.25:6 40:12 and by ἔλεος, Isa.47:6), Pro.26:22 (בֶּטֶן), Wis.10:5, Sir.30:7, 2Ma.9:5 (6), al. ;] 
the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): Acts.1:18. Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; see MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on Phil.1:8): 2 Cor.6:12 7:15, Phm 7 12 20, 1 John.3:17; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, Col.3:12; σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, Phil.2:1; σ. ἐλέους θεοῦ; ἡμῶν, Luke.1:78; σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Phil.1:8.†
 (AS)

G4699.d:
σπόγγος, -ου, ὁ 
 a sponge: Matt.27:48, Mark.15:36, John.19:29.†
 (AS)

G4700.d:
σποδός, -oῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for אֵפֶר ;] 
ashes: Heb.9:13; ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ. (Isa.58:5, John.3:6, Dan LXX 9:3, al.), Matt.11:21, Luke.10:13.†
 (AS)

G4701.d:
σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
 (σπείρω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (זָרַע), 1Ma.10:30 * ;] 
  1. a sowing. 
  2. seedtime. 
  3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): 1 Pet.1:23 
 (cf. σπέρμα, and see Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).†
 (AS)

G4702.d:
σπόριμος, -ον
 (σπείρω) [in LXX: Gen.1:29, Lev.11:37 (זָרַע), Sir 40:22 א1 * ;] 
fit for sowing, sown; as subst., τὰ σ., corn-fields: Matt.12:1, Mark.2:23, Luke.6:1.†
 (AS)

G4703.d:
σπόρος, -ου, ὁ
 (σπείρω), [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;] 
= σπορά, 
  1. sowing or seedtime. 
  2. seed sown (so usually in late Gk.): Mark.4:26-27, Luke.8:5, 11, 2 Cor.9:10 a (LTr.); metaphorically, of almsgiving, 2 Cor.9:10 b.†
 (AS)

G4704.d:
σπουδάζω
 (σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל ;] 
to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: with inf. (see M, Pr., 205 f.),  Gal.2:10, Eph.4:3, 1 Thess.2:17, 2 Tim.2:15 4:9 4:21, Titus.3:12, Heb.4:11, 2 Pet.1:10 3:14; with accusative and inf. (on this construction see Mayor in l; MM, xxiii), 2 Pet.1:15 (for other constructions see LS, see word).†
 (AS)

G4705.d:
σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον
 (σπουδή), [in LXX: Eze.41:25 * ;] 
in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: before ἐν, 2 Cor.8:22; compar., -οτεροσς 2 Cor.8:17 (here in superl. sense, see Bl., § 44, 3) 2 Cor.8:22.†
 (AS)

G4706.d: - more earnestly diligently, seriously, earnestly  than others), i.e. very promptly

G4708.d:
earnestly, zealously, with vigor; (compar.) all the more eager, with special urgency eagerly 
earnestly, eagerly, diligently, Lk. 7:4; 2 Timm. 1:17; Titus. 3:13; comparative σπουδαιοτέρως, more earnestly, with special urgency, Phil. 2:28

G4709.d:
σπουδαίως
  adv. (σπουδαῖος), [in LXX: Wis.2:6 * ;] 
  1. with haste or zeal, i.e. earnestly, zealously, diligently: Luke.7:4, 2 Tim.1:17, Titus.3:13; compar., -οτέρως, Phil.2:28 (RV, Lft., Weymouth, al., but see infr.) 
  2. hastily, speedily: compar., -οτέρως, Phil.2:28 (Thayer, Zorell, see word; ICC, in l, al., but see supr.).†
 (AS)

G4710.d:
σπουδή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (σπεύδω), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל, its parts and derivatives ;] 
  1. haste, speed: μετὰ σ. (Wis.19:2), Mark.6:25, Luke.1:39. 
  2. zeal, diligence, earnestness: Rom.12:11, 2 Cor.7:11-12 8:7-8; ἐν σ., Rom.12:8 (see M, Pr, 104); before ὑπέρ, 2 Cor.8:16; σπουδὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι, Heb.6:11; σ. παρεισφέρειν, 2 Pet.1:5; πᾶσαν σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Ju 3 (see MM, xxiii; M, Pr., 214; Deiss., BS, 361, 364).†
 (AS)

G4711.d:
σφυρίς (T, Rec. σπυρίς, see WH, App., 148; 131., § 6, 7), -ίδος, ἡ, 
 a flexible mat-basket for carrying provisions: Matt.15:37 16:10, Mark.8:8, 20 Acts.9:25 (see: κόφινος).†
 (AS)

G4712.d:
στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (John.6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (see B1., 9, 1), 
 [in LXX: Dan LXX 4:9, Sus 1:37, 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:9 ff. * ;] 
a stadium, i.e. 
  1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Matt.14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Luke.24:13, John.6:19 11:18, Rev.14:20 21:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course, 
  2. a race-course: 1 Cor.9:24.†
 (AS)

G4713.d:
στάρνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ 
 [in LXX: Exod.16:33 (צִנְצֶנֶת), 3Ki.12:24 14:3 (בַּקְבֻּק), Dan LXX Bel, 1:32 * ;] 
prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: Heb.9:4.†
 (AS)

G4714.d:
στάσις, -εως, ἡ
 (ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for עָמַד, its parts and derivatives, also for רִיב (Pr 1714), etc. (see Deiss., BS, 158 f.) ;] 
  1. a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν (Polyb., v, 5, 3; and cf. Lat. locum habere), Heb.9:8. 
  2. insurrection, sedition: Mark.15:7, Luke.23:19, 25, Acts.19:40 24:5. 
  3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension (cf. MM, xxiii) Acts.15:2 23:7, 10.†
 (AS)

G4716.d:
σταυρός, -oῦ, ὁ 
  1. an upright pale or stake (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.) 
  2. In late writers (Diod., Plut., al.) of the Roman instrument of crucifixion, the Cross: of the Cross on which Christ suffered, Matt.27:32, 40 27:42, Mark.15:21, 30 15:32, Luke.23:26, John.19:17, 19 19:25, 31, Col.2:14, Heb.12:2; θάνατος σταυροῦ, Phil.2:8; τ. αἷμα τοῦ σ., Col.1:20. Metaphorical, in proverbial sayings: αἴρειν (λαμβάνειν, βαστάζειν) τὸν σ., Matt.10:38 16:24, Mark.8:34 10:21,  15:21, Luke.9:23 14:27 (for an interesting ex. of metaphorically use in π., see MM, xxiii) By meton., for Christ's death on the Cross: 1 Cor.1:17, Gal.5:11 6:12, 14, Eph.2:16, Phil.3:18; ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σ., 1 Cor.1:18.†
 (AS)

G4717.d:
σταυρόω, -ῶ
 (σταυρός), [in LXX: Est.7:9 (תָּלָה), Est.8:13 * ;] 
  1. to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.). 
  2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: with accusative of person(s), Matt.20:19 23:34 26:2 27:22 ff. Matt.28:5, Mark.15:16 ff. Mark.16:6, Luke.23:21, 23 23:33 24:7, 20, John.19:6 ff., Acts.2:36 4:10, 1 Cor.1:13 1:23 2:2 2:8, 2 Cor.13:4, Gal.3:1, Rev.11:8; metaphorically, Gal.5:24 6:14.†
 (AS)

G4718.d:
σταφυλή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX for עֵנָב ;] 
a bunch of grapes: Matt.7:16, Luke.6:44, Rev.14:18. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opposite to ὄμφαξ, cf. Gen.40:10, Job.15:33; as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).†
 (AS)

G4719.d:
στάχυς, -υος, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for שִׁבֹּל ;] 
an ear of corn: Matt.12:1, Mark.2:23 4:28, Luke.6:1.†
 (AS)

G4720.d:
Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ 
 Stachys: Rom.16:9 (see Lft., Phi., 174; MM, xxiii).†
 (AS)

G4721.d:
στέγη, -ης, ἡ
 (στέγω) [in LXX: Gen.8:13 (מְכַסֶּה), etc. ;] 
a roof: Mark.2:4; of entering a house, εἰσέρχεσθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σ., Matt.8:8, Luke.7:6 (cf. MM, xxiii).†
 (AS)

G4722.d:
στέγω
 (cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Sir.8:17 * ;] 
  1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.). 
  2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Sir, l.with, Polyb., al.): 1 Cor.13:7, R, mg. 
  3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., see, Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): 1 Cor.9:12 13:7, 1 Thess.3:1 3:5.†
 (AS)

G4723.d:
στεῖρος, -ον also -α, -ον, 
 [in LXX for עָקָר ;] 
barren: of a woman, Luke.1:7, 36 23:29, Gal.4:27" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G4724.d:
στέλλω 
 [in LXX (mid.): Mal.2:5 (חָתַת ni.), Pro.31:24 (26), Wis.7:14 14:1, 2Ma.5:1, 3Ma.1:19 3Mac 4:11 * ;] 
  1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wis, xi Mac, ll. with). 
  2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: 2 Cor.8:20; before ἀπό, 2 Thess.3:6 
 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).†
 (AS)

G4725.d:
στέμμα, -τος, τό
 (στέφω, to put around, enwreath) 
a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Acts.14:13.†
 (AS)

G4726.d:
στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה, etc. ;] 
a groaning: Acts.7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Rom.8:26.†
 (AS)

G4727.d:
στενάζω 
 [in LXX for אָנַח ni., אָנַק, etc. ;] 
to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Mark.7:34, 2 Cor.5:2 5:4, Heb.13:17, Jas.5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Rom.8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).†
 SYN.: see: κλαίω  (AS)

G4728.d:
στενός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX for צַר, etc. ;] 
narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii), Matt.7:13-14, Luke.13:24.†
 (AS)

G4729.d:
στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ
 (στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Jos.17:15 (אוּץ), Jdg.16:16 (אָלַץ pi.), Isa.28:19 (20) (קָצַר) Isa.49:19 (צָרַר), 4Ma.11:11 * ;] 
  1. to be straitened (cf. Isa.49:19); metaphorically, to be anxious (Hipp., al.). 
  2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., 2 Cor.4:8 6:12.†
 (AS)

G4730.d:
στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.) 
 [in LXX for צוֹק, etc. ;] 
narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaphorical (Ken., Polyb., Deu.28:53, Wis.5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Rom.2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), 2 Cor.6:4 12:10.†
 SYN.: θλίψις, q.v  (AS)

G4731.d:
στερεός, -ά, -όν 
 [in LXX: Num.8:4 (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, Isa.5:28 (צַר), etc. ;] 
hard, firm, solid: τροψή, Heb.5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, figuratively, 2 Tim.2:19. Metaphorical, 
  (a) in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.); 
  (b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, 1 Pet.5:9.†
 (AS)

G4732.d:
στερεόω, -ῶ
 (στερεός), [in LXX: Isa.42:5 (רָקַע), Jer.5:3 (חָזַק pi.), etc. ;] 
  (a) to make firm or solid; 
  (b) to strengthen, make strong; with accusative of person(s), Acts.3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., Acts.3:7. Metaphorical (cf. Je, l.with): τ. πίστει, pass., Acts.16:5.†
 (AS)

G4735.d:
στέφανος, -ου, ὁ
 (στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה ;] 
  1. that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.). 
  2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, which see; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX for the golden crown of royalty (prop., διάδημα, which see, cf. Hort and Mayor on Jas.1:12): Matt.27:29, Mark.15:17, John.19:2, 5, 1 Cor.9:25, Rev.4:4, 10 6:2 9:7 12:1 14:14. Metaphorical: Phil.4:1, Rev.3:11; τ. δικαιοσύνης (cf. Deiss., LAE, 312), 2 Tim.4:8; τ. δόξης, 1 Pet.5:4; καυχήσεως, 1 Thess.2:19 (see M, Th., in l); τ. ζωῆς (genitive appos.), Jas.1:12, Rev.2:10.†
 (AS)

G4737.d:
στεφανόω, -ῶ
 (στέφανος), [in LXX for עָטַר ;] 
with accusative of person(s), 
 to crown: of a victor, 2 Tim.2:5. Metaphorical, δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, Heb.2:7, 9" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G4738.d:
στῆθος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX: Exod.28:23, 26 (29-30) (לֵב), etc. ;] 
the breast: John.13:25 21:10, Rev.15:6; as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ., Luke.18:13 23:48,†
 (AS)

G4739.d:
στήκω  late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (see B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii), 
 [in LXX: Exod.14:13 A, Jdg.16:26 B, 3Ki.8:11 B * ;] 
= ἵστημι, to stand: Mark.3:31 11:25, John.1:26, Rev.12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaphorical, to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Gal.5:1 (but see Field, Notes, 189 f.), 2 Thess.2:15; before ἐν, John.8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), 1 Cor.16:13, Phil.1:27 4:1; with dative, Rom.14:4.†
 (AS)

G4740.d:
στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Isa.3:1 * ;] 
  1. a setting firmly, supporting. 
  2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: 2 Pet.3:17.†
 (AS)

G4741.d:
στηρίζω 
 [in LXX for סָמַךְ, שׂוּם, etc. ;] 
to fix, set fast, make fast: Luke.16:26; τ. πρόσωτον (Eze.6:2 13:17, al.; see Dalman, Words, 30 f.), Luke.9:51. Metaphorical, to confirm, establish: with, accusative, Luke.22:32, Acts.18:23, Rom.1:11 16:25, 1 Thess.3:2 3:13, 2 Thess.3:3, Jas.5:8, 1 Pet.5:10, Rev.3:2; id. before ἐν, 2 Thess.2:17, 2 Pet.1:12.†
 (AS)

G4742.d:
στίγμα -τος, τό
 (στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Sng.1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;] 
a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Gal.6:17 (see Lft., in l; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).†
 (AS)

G4743.d:
στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Isa.29:5 (פֶּתַע), 2Ma.9:11 * ;] 
a prick, a point; metaphorically, σ. χρόνου, a moment: Luke.4:5.†
 (AS)

G4744.d:
στίλβω 
 [in LXX: Nam.3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;] 
to shine, glisten: Mark.9:3.†
 (AS)

G4745.d:
στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Eze.40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;] 
a portico: John.5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), John.10:23 Acts.3:11 5:12 †
 (AS)

G4746.d:
στοιβάς, see: στιβάς.
  στιβάς, -άδος, ἡ, 
 [in Aq.: Eze.46:23 (טִירוֺת) * ;] 
a litter of leaves or rushes: pl., Mark.11:8 (Rec. στοιβ-).†
 (AS)

G4747.d:
στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX: Wis.7:17 19:18, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] 
prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence, 
  1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.). 
  2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.). 
  3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Heb.5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Gal.4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Gal.4:3, Col.2:8, 20 (but see infr.). 
  4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2 Pet.3:10 3:12. 
  5. The heavenly bodies (Ding. Laert.). 
  6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. with, see ICC on Col.2:8; Enc. Bibl., see word " Elements ").†
 (AS)

G4748.d:
στοιχέω, -ῶ
 (στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ecc.11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;] 
to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: Acts.21:24; with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Rom.4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Gal.5:25 6:16, Phil.3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).†
 (AS)

G4749.d:
στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (στέλλω), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבוּשׁ, etc. ;] 
  1 1, an equipment, an armament (Æsch.). 
  2. Equipment  in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jon.3:6, Est.8:15, 1Ma.6:15): Mark.12:38 16:5, Luke.15:22 20:46, Rev.6:11 7:9, 13-14 22:14.†
 (AS)

G4750.d:
στόμα, -τος, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for פֻּם ;] 
the mouth: of man, Matt.15:11, John.19:29, Acts.11:8, al.; of animals, Matt.17:27, 2 Tim.4:17 (fig.), Heb.11:33, Jas.3:3, al.; figuratively, of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Rev.12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. חֶרֶב ־פֶּה, Gen.34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Luke.21:24, Heb.11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opposite to καρδία, Matt.12:34, Rom.10:8, 10; in various phrases (some cl., some resembling Hebrew; cf. Bl., § 40, 9): ἀνοίγειν τ. σ. (see: ἀνοίγω); σ. πρὸς σ. (פֶּה ־אֵל פֶּה Num.12:8; = cl., κατὰ σ., Hdt., al.), face to face, II Jn 12, 3 John.14; διὰ τοῦ σ. (of the Holy Spirit), Luke.1:70, Acts.1:16, al.; ἀπὸ (ἐκ) τοῦ σ. (cf. ἀπὸ σ. εἰπεῖν, Plat., al.), of speaking by word of mouth, Luke.22:71, Acts.22:14; δόλος (ψεῦδος) ἐν τ. σ., 1 Pet.2:22, Rev.14:5" (LXX) ; metaphorically, ἡ ῥομφαία τοῦ σ., Rev.2:16. By meton., for speech (Soph.): Matt.18:16 (LXX), Luke.19:22 21:15, 2 Cor.13:1 
 (AS)

G4752.d:
στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ 
 (οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] 
an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2 Cor.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1 Tim.1:18.†
 (AS)

G4753.d:
στράτευμα, -τος, τό
 (στρατεύω), [in LXX: 1Ma.9:34, 2Ma.5:24 2Mac 8:21 2Mac 12:38 2Mac 13:13; pl., Jdth.11:8, 4Ma.5:1 * ;] 
  1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.). 
  2. an army, a host: pl., Matt.22:7, Rev.9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Acts.23:10, 27; pl., Luke.23:11.†
 (AS)

G4754.d:
στρατεύω  and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT 
 (στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23 ;] 
used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Luke.3:14, 1 Cor.9:7, 2 Tim.2:4. Metaphorical (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: 2 Cor.10:3, 1 Tim.1:18, Jas.4:1, 1 Pet.2:11.†
 (AS)

G4755.d:
στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (στραός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;] 
  1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.). 
  2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Acts.16:20, 22 16:35-36, 38. 
  3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Acts.4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Luke.22:4, 52.†
 SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Acts.16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217).  (AS)

G4756.d:
στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] 
  1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (3Ki.22:19, al.), Luke.2:13; of the stars of heaven (Jer.8:2, 2Ch.33:3), Acts.7:42. 
  2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: 2 Cor.10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).†
 (AS)

G4757.d:
στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX; 2Ki.23:8 B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac 14:39, III Mac  3:12; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 * ;] 
a soldier: Matt.8:9, Mark.15:16, John.19:2, Acts.10:7, al.; metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., 2 Tim.2:3.†
 (AS)

G4758.d:
στρατολογέω, -ῶ
 (στρατός, λέγω), 
to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: 2 Tim.2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).†
 (AS)

G4759.d:
στρατοπέδ-αρχος (Rec. -ης), -ου, ὁ 
 (στρατόπεδον, ἄρχω), a military commander, esp. the Pretorian prefect: Acts.28:16 (WH, om.).† 
στρατοπεδάρχης, see: στρατοπέδαρχος 
 (AS)

G4760.d:
στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό
 (στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Jer.34:1 (חַיִל), 2Ma.8:12, al. ;] 
  (a) a military camp; 
  (b) an army: Luke.21:20.†
 (AS)

G4761.d:
στρεβλόω, -ῶ
 (στρέφω), [in LXX: 2Ki.22:27 (פָּתַל hithp.), 3Ma.4:14, 4Ma.9:17 4Mac 12:4 4Mac 12:11 4Mac 15:14 * ;] 
to twist, torture. Metaphorical (cf. 2Ki, l.with), to twist or pervert language: 2 Pet.3:16.†
 (AS)

G4762.d:
στρέφω 
 [in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ, also for סָבַב, etc. ;] 
to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), Matt.5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Matt.27:3 (cf. Isa.38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Acts.7:42; with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Rev.11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: before εἰς, John.20:14, Acts.7:39 13:46; ptcp., στραφείς, with indic., Matt.7:6 9:22 16:23, Luke.7:9 9:55 14:25 22:61, John.1:38 20:16; id. before πρός, Luke.7:44 10:22 (WH, R, om.), Luke.7:23 23:28; metaphorically, to change: absol., Matt.18:3, John.12:40 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στρέφω).†
 (AS)

G4763.d:
στρηνιάω, ῶ
 (στρῆνος, which see), [in Sm.: Isa.61:6 (אָכַל) * ;] 
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Rev.18:7-9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
 SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), τρυφάω  (AS)

G4764.d:
στρῆνος, -ους, τό
 (cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;] 
insolent luxury, wantonness: Rev.18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†
 (AS)

G4765.d:
στρουθίον, -ου, τό

στυγητός, -όν

στυγνάζω

G4769.d:

G4771.d:
σύ, 
 pron. of 2nd of person(s), 
thou, you, genitive, σοῦ, dative, σοί, accusative, σέ, pl., ὑμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς (enclitic in oblique cases sing., except after prep. (BL, §48, 3), though πρὸς σέ occurs in Matt.25:39). Nom. for emphasis or contrast: John.1:30, 4:10, 5:33, 39, 44, Acts.4:7, Eph.5:32; so also perhaps σὺ εἶπας, Matt.26:64, al. (M, Pr., 86); before voc., Matt.2:6, Luke.1:76, John.17:5, al.; sometimes without emphasis (M, Pr., 85f.), as also in cl., but esp. as rendering of Heb. phrase, e.g. υἱός μου εἶ σύ (בְּנִי־אַתָּה, Ps.2:7), Acts.13:33.  (AS)

 SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (which see) (AS)

G4774.d:
συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ
 (συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Sir prol.14 (B1N1 cm.) 313, 2Mac 14:20* ;]

G4775.d:
συν-κάθημαι
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Ps.101:6 (יָשַׁב) * ;]

περι-καθ-ίζω

G4778.d:
συν-κακουχέομαι (Rec. συγκ-), -οῦμαι, pass.

G4779.d:
συν-καλέω
 (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, [in LXX for קָרָא ;] 
to call together: with accusative, Mark.15:16, Luke.15:6, 9 (seel. -εῖται, see B1., § 55, 1), Acts.5:21. Mid., to call together to oneself: Luke.9:1 (and seel. in Luke.15:6, 9 see supr.) Luke.23:13, Acts.10:24 28:17.†

G4781.d:
συν-κάμπτω
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Ps.68:10, 23 (מעד hi.), etc. ;] 
to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, Rom.11:10 (LXX).†

G4782.d:
συν-κατα-βαίνω
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Ps.49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 * ;]

G4783.d:
συν-κατά-θεσις (Rec συγκ-), -εως, ἡ

G4784.d:
συν-κατα-τίθημι
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Exod.23:1 (שִׁית יָד), Exod.23:32 (בְּרִית), Da TH Su 1:20 * ;]

συν-κεράννυμι
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:43 (עֲרַב ithpa.), 2Ma.15:39 * ;] 
to mix or blend together, compound: with accusative, 1 Cor.12:24; ptcp. pf. pass., Heb.4:2, T, WH, mg., R, mg.; id., of persons, with dative instr., to be united with, agree with, ib., WH, txt., R, txt. (see Westc., in l).†

G4787.d:
συν-κινέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, 
 to move together. Metaphorical, to excite, stir up: τ. λαόν, Acts.6:12 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

G4788.d:
συν-κλείω

G4789.d:
συν-κληρο-νόμος (Rec. συγκ-), -ου, ὁ

G4790.d:
συν-κοινωνέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, 
 to have fellowship with or in (in cl., with genitive of thing(s), dative of person(s)): with dative of thing(s), Eph.5:11, Rev.18:4; id. with genitive of person(s), Phil.4:14.†

συν-κοινωνός (Rec. συγκ-), όν,

συν-κομίζω
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.5:26 (עָלָה) * ;]

συλ-λογίζομαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב pi. ;]

συμ-βουλεύω

συν-παθέω
 (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: 4Ma.5:25 AR 4Ma.13:23 * ;] 
to have a fellow feeling for or with, sympathize with or in: with dative of thing(s), Heb.4:15; dative of person(s), Heb.10:34 (Arist., Plut., al.).†
 (AS)

G4835.d:
συμπαθής, -ές
 (σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Job.29:25 A (אָבֵל), 4Ma.5:25 א, 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 15:4 * ;] 
  1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: 1 Pet.3:8. 
  2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.with; Dion. H.).†
 (AS)

G4836.d:
συν-παρα-γίνομαι
 (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Ps.83:8 (לָוָה ni.) * ;] 
  1. to come up or be present together: before ἐπί, Luke.23:48. 
  2. to come up to assist (Thuc., al.; 2 Tim.4:16, Rec.).†
 (AS)

G4837.d:
συν-παρα-καλέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, 
 to call upon or exhort together (Plat.). Pass., to be strengthened or comforted with and among: Rom.1:12.†
 (AS)

G4838.d:
συν-παρα-λαμβάνω
 (Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Gen.19:17 (סָפָה ni.), Job.1:4 (שָׁלַח ni), 3Ma.1:1 * ;] 
to take along with: as a companion, with accusative, Acts.12:25 15:37-38 (on the tenses, see M, Pr., 130), Gal.2:1.†
 (AS)

G4839.d:
συμ-παρα-μένω 
 Rec, for παρα-μένω (which see), Phil.1:25.†
 (AS)

G4840.d:
συν-πάρειμι
 (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 * ;] 
to be present together or with: with dative of person(s), Acts.25:24.†
 (AS)

G4841.d:
συν-πάσχω
 (Rec. συμπ-), [in Al.: 1Ki.22:8 * ;] 
  1. to suffer together or with: Rom.8:17, 1 Cor.12:28. 
  2. to sympathize with (Plat., Arist.).†
 (AS)

G4842.d:
συν-πέμπω (Rec. συμπ-) 
 to send together with: with accusative and dative, 2 Cor.8:22; id. before μετά, with genitive, 2 Cor.8:18.†
 (AS)

G4843.d:
συν-περι-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-), 
  1. to enclose (Eze.5:3 (צוּר) *). 
  2. to embrace: with accusative of person(s), Acts.20:10.†
 (AS)

G4844.d:
συμπόσιον, -ου, τό
 (συμπίνω), [in LXX: Est.7:7 (מִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן) Est.4:17, 1Ma.16:16, 2Ma.2:27, 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:36 3Mac 6:33; σ. οἴνου, Sir 34:31 (31:31) Sir.35:5 (32:5), Sir.49:1 * ;] 
  1. a drinking party 
  2. By meton., of the party itself, the guests (Plut); pl., σ. σ. (colloq.; see M, Pr., 97), in parties or companies: Mark.6:39.†
 (AS)

G4845.d:
συν-πληρόω
 (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Jer.25:12 (נָפַל) * ;] 
  1. to fill up completely (Thuc., of manning ships): of a ship filling with water, and by meton., of those on board, Luke.8:23. 
  2. to complete, fulfil: of time (Je, l.with, and see MM, xxiv), Luke.9:51, Acts.2:1 (on the "durative inf.," see M, Pr., 233).†
 (AS)

G4846.d:
συν-πνίγω (Rec. συμπ-), 
 to choke: of thronging by a crowd, Luke.8:42. Fig., of seed, τ. λόγον, Matt.13:22, Mark.4:7, 19, Luke.8:14.†
 (AS)

G4847.d:
συν-πολίτης (Rec. σνμπ-), -ου, ὁ 
 a fellow-citizen: pl., σ. τ. ἁγίων, opposite to ξένοι κ. πάροικοι, Eph.2:19 (Eur.; C.I., 6446; condemned by Atticists; see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).†
 (AS)

G4848.d:
συν-πορεύομαι
 (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ ;] 
  1. to journey together (Plat., al.): with dative of person(s), Luke.7:11 14:25 24:15. 
  2. to come together: Mark.10:1 (Plut., al.).†

G4849.d:

G4850.d:
συν-πρεσβύτερος (Rec. συμπ-), -ου, ὁ 
 a fellow-elder: 1 Pet.5:1 (Eccl.).†

συμ-φέρω

  1. trans. to bring together: with accusative of thing(s), Acts.19:19. 
  2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: 1 Cor.6:12 10:23, 2 Cor.8:10; with inf. (M, Pr., 210), Matt.19:10, John.18:14; with dative, before ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 5), Matt.5:29-30 18:6, John.11:50 16:7. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: 1 Cor.12:7; pl., Acts.20:20; (οὐ σ. sc. ἐστιν; = οὐ συμφέρει; cf. Thuc., iii, 44, 2), 2 Cor.12:1; as subst., τὸ σ., profit, Heb.12:10.†
 (AS)

G4852.d:
σύν φημι (Rec. συμ-), 
 to consent, confess: with dative, before ὅτι, Rom.7:16.†
 (AS)

G4853.d:
συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ
 (σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Zec.13:7; and see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.) 
a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: 1 Thess.2:14 (see M, Th., in l, and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.†
 (AS)

G4854.d:
σύμ-φυτος, -ον
 (συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: Zec.11:2 (בָּצַר), Est.7:7 Est.7:8 א2, Amo.9:13, 3Ma.3:22 * ;] 
  1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; 3Mac, l.with). 
  2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (see Field, Notes, 155 f.), Rom.6:5.†
 (AS)

G4855.d:
συν-φύω
 (Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Wis.13:13 * ;] 
to cause to grow together. Pass., to grow together or with (Plat. al.): Luke.8:7.†
 (AS)

G4856.d:
συμ-φωνέω, -ῶ, 
 [in LXX: Gen.14:3 (H2266) 2Ki.12:8 (9) (H225 ni.), Isa.7:2 (H5117), 4Ma.14:6 * ;] 
prop., to agree in sound, be in harmony (Plat., Arist.). Metaphorical, 
  (a) to agree with, agree together: Luke.5:36; with dative of thing(s), Acts.15:15; before περί, Matt.18:19; pass., with dative of person(s), συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν, Acts.5:9; 
  (b) to agree as to a price (Polyb., Diod.): with dative of person(s), genitive pret., Matt.20:13; before μετά . . . ἐκ, Matt.20:2.†
 (AS)

G4857.d:
συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ
 (συμφωνέω), 
concord, agreement: before πρός, with accusative of person(s), 2 Cor.6:15.†
 (AS)

G4858.d:
συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ
 (σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15,  TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A * ;] 
  1. symphony, music: Luke.15:25 
  2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. with; v MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G4859.d:
σύμφωνος, -ον
 (ούν, φωνή), [in LXX: Ecc.7:14 (עֻמָּה), 4Ma.7:7 4Mac 14:7 * ;] 
agreeing in sound. Metaphorical, harmonious, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου (for exx. from π., see Deiss., BS, 255), by agreement, 1 Cor.7:5.†
 (AS)

G4860.d:
συμ-ψηφίζω 
 [in LXX: Jer.29:20 (Jer.49:20) A * ;] 
to reckon together, count up: Acts.19:19.†
 (AS)

G4861.d:
σύν-ψυχος (Rec. συμ-), -ον 
 (ψυχή), 
of one mind: Phil.2:2.†
 (AS)

G4862.d:
σύν (old Att. ξύν), 
 prep. with dative,  
expressing association, fellowship and inclusion. It gradually gave way to μετά, with genitive (cf. LS, see word; Bl., §41, 3), and is therefore comparatively infrequent in NT, being rare in Mat.4, Mrk.6, Jhn.3, and elsewhere (exx. Jas.1:11, 2 Pet.1:18) only in Lk (Gosp. and Ac) and Paul. With, together with: of companionship and association, Luke.2:13, John.21:3, Acts.10:23, al.; εἶναι σύν τινι, Luke.7:12, Acts.4:13, Phil.1:23, al.; of partisanship, Acts.4:13; οἱ σύν τινι, of attendants, companions or colleagues, Mark.2:26, Luke.5:9, Acts.5:17, al.; of assistance, ἡ χάρις τ. θεοῦ σὺν ἐμοί, 1 Cor.15:10; of two or more things together, almost = καί, Luke.23:11, Acts.3:4 10:2 14:5 23:25, Eph.3:18; σὺν Χριστῷ ζῆν, 2 Cor.13:4; besides (FlJ, LXX), σὺν πᾶσι τούτοις, Luke.24:21. In composition: with (συνχαίρω), together (συνωδίνω), altogether (συντελέω) 
 (AS)

G4863.d:
συν-άγω 
 [in LXX chiefly for אָסַף, also for קָבַץ, etc. (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 128) ;] 
to gather or bring together: of things, John.6:12-13; before εἰς, Matt.3:12, al.; ἐκεῖ, Luke.12:18; ποῦ, Luke.12:17; συναγαγὼν πάντα (sc. εἰς ἀργύριον; see Field, Notes, 68, MM, xxiv), having sold off all: Luke.15:13; of persons, John.11:52; esp. of assemblies, Matt.2:4, John.11:47, Acts.14:27, al. Pass., to be gathered or come together: Matt.22:41, Mark.2:2, Luke.22:66, al.; before ἐπί Mark.5:21, Acts.4:27; πρός, Matt.13:2, Mark.4:1, al.; εἰς, Rev.19:17; ἐν, Acts.11:26; μετά, Matt.28:12; οὗ, Matt.18:20; ὅπου, Matt.26:57; ἐκεῖ, John.18:2, al. 
 In late writers (see Kennedy, Sources, 128; cf. Deu.22:2, al.), to receive hospitably, entertain: Matt.25:35, 38 25:43 (cf. ἐπι-συνάγω) 
 (AS)

G4865.d:
συν-αγωνίζομαι 
 to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): with dative of person(s) and of thing(s), Rom.15:30.†

G4866.d:
συν-αθλέω, -ῶ 
 = συναγωνίζομαι: with dative commod., Phil.1:27; with dative of person(s), before ἐν, Phil.4:3.†

G4867.d:
συν-αθροίζω

 ἀθροίζω

to Gather, assemble: Luke.24:33.†

G4868.d:
συν-αίρω 
 [in LXX: Exod.23:5 (עָזַב) * ;]

G4869.d:
συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ

 (AS)

G4870.d:
συν-ακολουθέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 2:6 * ;] 
to follow along with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Mark.14:51, Luke.23:49; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Mark.5:37.†
 (AS)

G4871.d:
συν-αλίζω 
 [in Al.: Ps.141:4 * ;] 
to assemble with: Acts.1:4 (EV, mg., eating with, but on this rendering and on the force of the Pres. ptcp. here, see Field, Notes, 110).†
 (AS)

G4872.d:
συν-ανα-βαίνω 
 [in LXX for עָלָה ;] 
to go up with: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., Mark.15:41, Acts.13:31.†
 (AS)

G4873.d:
συν-ανά-κειμαι 
 [in LXX: 3Ma.5:39 * ;] 
to recline with or together at table: Matt.14:9, Mark.6:22, Luke.7:49 14:15; with dative of person(s), Matt.9:10, Mark.2:15, Luke.14:10.†

G4874.d:
συν-ανα-μίγνυμι
 (accusative to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), [in LXX: Hos.7:8 A ( hithpo.), Eze.20:18 A * ;] 
to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaphorically, to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): 1 Cor.5:9 5:11, 2 Thess.3:14 (see M, Th., 117).†

G4875.d:
συν-ανα-παύομαι 
 [in LXX: Isa.11:6 (רָבַץ) * ;] 
with dative of person(s), to lie down to rest with, sleep with. Metaphorical, to be refreshed in spirit with: Rom.15:32 (L, om.).†

G4876.d:
συν-αντάω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX for פָּגַע, פָּגַשׁ, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc. ;] 
to meet with: with dative of person(s), Luke.9:18, 37 22:10, Acts.10:25, Heb.7:1, 10. Metaphorical, of events, to happen, befall (Ding. L., Plut., al.): Acts.20:22.†
 (AS)

G4877.d:
συν-άντησις, -εως, ἡ 
 Rec. for ὑπάντησις (which see), Matt.8:34.†
 (AS)

G4878.d:
συν-αντι-λαμβάνομαι 
 [in LXX: Gen.30:8 R (†), Exod.18:22, Num.11:17 (נָשָׂא), Ps.89:21 (כּוּן ni.) * ;] 
to take hold with at the side for assistance; hence, to take a share in, help in bearing, and generally, help (with various constructions, see LXX, ll. with, Deiss., LAE, 83 f.): with dative, Luke.10:40, Rom.8:26.†
 (AS)

G4879.d:
συν-απ-άγω 
 [in LXX: Exod.14:6 (לָקַח) * ;] 
to lead away with or together (Ex, l.with). Pass., metaphorically (as συμπεριφέρομαι, see LS, see word), to be carried away with: with dative, Gal.2:13, 2 Pet.3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163), Rom.12:16.†
 (AS)

G4880.d:
συν-απο-θνήσκω 
 [in LXX: Sir.19:10 * ;] 
to die with or together: Mark.14:31, 2 Cor.7:3 (see Meyer, in l), 2 Tim.2:11.†
 (AS)

G4881.d:
συν-απ-όλλυμι 
 [in LXX chiefly for סָפָה ;] 
to destroy with or together. Pass., to perish together (with): with dative of person(s), Heb.11:31.†
 (AS)

G4882.d:
συν-απο-στέλλω 
 [in LXX: Exod.33:2, 12 (שָׁלַח), I Est.5:2 * ;] 
to send along with: with accusative, 2 Cor.12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G4883.d:
συν-αρμολογέω, -ῶ
 (ἁρμός, λέγω), = cl. συναρμόζω, 
to fit or frame  together: of the parts of a building, Eph.2:21; of the members of the body, Eph.4:16 (Eccl.).†
 (AS)

G4884.d:
συν-αρπάζω 
 [in LXX: Pro.6:25 (לָקַח), 2Ma.3:27 2Mac 4:41, 4Ma.5:4 * ;] 
"perfective " of ἁοπάζω (see M, Pr., 113), 
  (a) to seize and carry away (so most commonly) : Acts.27:15;

G4885.d:
συν-αυξάνω 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.13:27 * ;] 
to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Matt.13:30 (Xen., al.).†
 (AS)

G4887.d:
συν-δέω 
 [in LXX for שָׁבַץ, etc. ;] 
  (a) to bind together;

 (AS)

G4888.d:
συν-δοξάζω

  2. In NT only, to glorify together: pass., Rom.8:17.†
 (AS)

G4889.d:
σύν-δουλος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Est.4:7, 9 4:17, 23 5:3, 6 6:6, 13 (כְּנָת) * ;] 
a fellow-servant: Matt.18:28-33 24:49; of servants of the same divine Lord, Col.1:7 4:7, Rev.6:11; so of angels, Rev.19:10 22:9.†
 (AS)

G4890.d:
συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jdth.10:18, 3Ma.3:8 * ;] 
concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Acts.21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†
 (AS)

G4891.d:
συν-εγείρω 
 [in LXX: Exod.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 * ;] 
to raise together: metaphorically, of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph.2:6; pass., Col.2:12 3:1.†

G4892.d:
συνέδριον, -ου, τό
 (σύν + ἕδρα, a seat) [in LXX: Pro.11:13 15:22, Jer.15:17 (סוֹד), Ps.26:4 (מַת), Pro.22:10 (דִּין) Pro.26:26 (קָהָל); Pro.24:7 27:22 31:23, 2Ma.14:5, 4Ma.17:17 * ;]

The supreme ecclesiastical court of the Jews, the Sanhedrin (i.e. Talmudic סַנְהֵדְרִין = συνέδριον): Matt.5:22 26:59, Mark.14:55 15:1, Luke.22:66, Acts.5:21, 27 5:34, 41 6:12, 15 22:30 23:1, 6 23:15, 20 23:28 (WH, R, mg., om.) Acts.24:20 of a meeting of the Sanhedrin, John.11:47; of the place of meeting, Acts.4:15.†
 (AS)

G4893.d:
συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ
 (συνεῖδον), [in LXX: Ecc.10:20 (מַדָּע), Wis.17:11, Sir.42:18 א * ;] 
  1. consciousness: with genitive obj., Heb.10:2, 1 Pet.2:19. 
  2. Cremer, 233 ff.; ICC on Rom.2:15; DB, i, 468 ff.).†
 (AS)

G4894.d:
συν-εῖδον  irreg. aorist of συνοράω (see: εἶδον), 
 [in LXX: 1Ma.4:21 א, 2Ma.2:24 2Mac 4:4 2Mac 4:41 R 2Ma.5:17 2Mac 7:4 2Mac 7:20 2Mac 8:8, 3Ma.2:8 A * ;]

 (AS)

G4895.d:
σύν-ειμι
 (εἰμί to be), [in LXX: Jer.3:20 (רֵעַ), al. ;] 
to be with: Luke.9:18 (WH, mg., συνήντησαν), Acts.22:11.†
 (AS)

G4896.d:
σύν-ειμι
 (εἶμι, to go), 
to come together: Luke.8:4.†
 (AS)

G4897.d:
συν-εισ-έρχομαι 
 [in LXX: Job.22:4 (עִם בּוֹא), etc. ;] 
to enter together: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., John.6:22 18:15.†
 (AS)

G4898.d:
συν-έκδημος, -ου, ὁ
 (ἔκδημος, abroad), 
a fellow-traveller: Acts.19:29, 2 Cor.8:1.†
 (AS)

G4899.d:
συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν 
 chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, see ICC, in l), 1 Pet.5:13.†
 (AS)

G4900.d:
συν-ελαύνω 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.4:26 2Mac 4:42 2Mac 5:5 * ;] 
to drive together, force together: εἰς εἰρήνην, Acts.7:26, Rec. (WH, RV, συνήλλασσεν).†
 (AS)

G4901.d:
συν-επι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ 
 to join in attesting, bear witness together with: Heb.2:4 (Arist., Polyb., a1.).†
 (AS)

G4902.d:
συν-έπομαι 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.15:2, 3Ma.5:48 R 3Ma.6:21 * ;] 
to follow with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Acts.20:4.†
 (AS)

G4903.d:
συνεργέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: I Est.7:2, 1Ma.12:1 * ;] 
  1. prop., to work together (with): absol., Mark.16:20, 1 Cor.16:16, 2 Cor.6:1; with dative, Jas.2:22; dative commod., Rom.8:28, T, R, txt. (but see infr.). 
  2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together (cf. ICC, in l): with accusative of thing(s), Rom.8:28 [WH] R, mg. (but see supr.).†
 (AS)

G4904.d:
συνεργός, -όν 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.8:7 Mac 14:5 * ;] 
a fellow-worker: with genitive of person(s), Rom.16:3, 9 16:21, Phil.2:25 4:3, 1 Thess.3:2, Rec., Phm 1 24; θεοῦ (cf. Lft., Notes, 41, 188), 1 Cor.3:9 (pl.), 1 Thess.3:2 [WH] R, mg. (R, txt., διάκονον τοῦ θ.; on the original reading, see ICC, in l); τ. χαρᾶς ὑηῶν, 2 Cor.1:24; τ. ἀληθείᾳ, III Jn 8; before εἰς, 2 Cor.8:23, Col.4:11.†
 (AS)

συν-έρχομαι 
 [in LXX for הָלַךְ, בּוֹא, אָסַף ni., etc. ;] 
  1. (cl.) to come together, assemble: Mark.3:20 14:53, T, WH, txt., Acts.1:6 2:6 10:27 16:13 19:32 21:22 22:30 28:17, 1 Cor.14:26; before εἰς, with accusative loc., Acts.5:16; ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, 1 Cor.11:20 14:23; with dative of person(s), Mark.14:53, WH, mg., R (πρὸς αὐτόν, see Field, Notes, 40), John.11:33; ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, 1 Cor.11:18; ἐνθάδε, Acts.25:17; Mark.6:33, WH, mg.   2. In later sense (see exx. in Milligan, Selections, 64, 105), to accompany: with dative of person(s), Luke.23:55, Acts.1:21 9:39 10:23, 45 11:12; before σύν, Acts.21:16; εἰς, Acts.15:38.†
