G4906.d:
συν-εσθίω 
 [in LXX: Gen.43:32, Exod.18:12 (אָכַל), 4Ki.12:17 (בָּרָה), Ps.101:5 * ;] 
to eat with one: with dative of person(s), Luke.15:2, Acts.10:41 11:3, 1 Cor.5:11; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Gal.2:12.†
 (AS)

G4907.d:
σύνεσις, -εως, ἡ
 (συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּינָה and cogn. forms, מַשְׂכִּית, דַּעַת, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;] 
  1. a running or flowing together (Hom.). 
  2. (a) understanding: Luke.2:47, 1 Cor.1:19" (LXX), Eph.3:4, Col.1:9 2:2, 2 Tim.2:7 
  (b) the understanding, the mind or intelligence: Mark.12:33.†
 SYN.: see: σοφία  (AS)

G4908.d:
συνετός, ή, -όν
 (συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם, etc. ;] 
intelligent, sagacious, understanding: Matt.11:25, Luke.10:21, Acts.13:7, 1 Cor.1:19" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G4909.d:
συν-ευ-δοκέω, -ῶ
 [in LXX: 1Ma.1:57, 1Ma.4:28 א1, 2Ma.11:24 2Mac 11:35 * ;] 
to join in approving, consent, agree to or with: absol., Acts.22:20; with dative of person(s), Rom.1:32; with dative of thing(s), Luke.11:48, Acts.8:1; with inf., 1 Cor.7:12-13 (chiefly in late writers).† 
 (AS)

G4910.d:
συν-ευωχέω, -ῶ 
 to entertain together. Pass., to fare sumptuously or feast together or with: Ju 12; with dative of person(s), 2 Pet.2:13 (Arist., Luc., al.).†
 (AS)

G4911.d:
συν-εφ-ίστημι 
 to place over. Pass., 
  1. to stand over (Thuc.). 
  2. to rise together: before κατά, with genitive of person(s) (against), Acts.16:22.†
 (AS)

G4912.d:
συν-έχω 
 [in LXX for עָצָר, חָבַר, etc. ;] 
  1. to hold together (τ. συνέχον τ. πάντα, Wis.1:7): of closing the ears, Acts.7:57 (τ. στόμα, Isa.52:15); to hem in, press on every side: Luke.8:45 19:43. 
  2. to hold fast; 
  (a) of a prisoner, to hold in charge (Luc.; cf. exx. in Deiss., BS, 160; MM, xxiv): Luke.22:63; 
  (b) to constrain: 2 Cor.5:14; pass., Luke.12:50, Acts.18:5 (τ. λόγῳ; cf. Field, Notes, 128), Phil.1:23; in pass., of ills, to be seized or afflicted by, suffering from: Matt.4:24, Luke.4:38 8:37, Acts.28:8.†
 (AS)

G4913.d:
συν-ήδομαι 
 to rejoice together; with dative, to rejoice with or in: τ. νόμῳ τ. θεοῦ, Rom.7:22 (see Lft., Notes, 304).†
 (AS)

G4914.d:
συνήθεια, -ας, ἡ
 (ἦθος), [in LXX: 4Ma.2:12 4Mac 6:13 4Mac 13:22 4Mac 13:27 * ;] 
  1 1 intimacy. 
  2. habit, custom: John.18:39, 1 Cor.11:16; with genitive obj. (cf. Æschin., 23, 37, and see MM, xxiv), habitual use, force of habit with respect to, 1 Cor.8:7.†
 (AS)

G4915.d:
συν-ηλικιώτης
 (ἡλικία), = συνῆλιζ (Æsch.), 
one of the same age, an equal in age: Gal.1:14.†
 (AS)

G4916.d:
συν-θάπτω 
 to bury together with: in symbolical sense, of baptism, σὐτῷ (with Christ), Rom.6:4, Col.2:12.†
 (AS)

G4917.d:
συν-θλάω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX for מָחַץ etc. ;] 
to crush together, crush: Matt.21:44 ([WH], R, mg., om.), Luke.20:18.†
 (AS)

G4918.d:
συν-θλίβω 
 [in LXX: Ecc.12:6 א A (רָצַץ), Sir.34:14 (31:14), 1Ma.15:14 A * ;] 
to press together, press on all sides: Mark.5:24, 31.†
 (AS)

G4919.d:
συν-θρύπτω 
 to break in pieces, crush: metaphorically, τ. καρδίαν, Acts.21:13.†
 (AS)

G4920.d:
συν-ίημι and συνίω (see Bl., § 23, 7), 
 [in LXX chiefly for בִּין hi., שָׂכַל hi. ;] 
  1. to bring or set together. 
  2. Metaphorical, to perceive, understand: Matt.13:13-15 (LXX), Matt.13:19 15:10, Mark.4:9 (WH, mg.), Mark.4:12 7:14 8:17, 21 Luke.8:10, Acts.7:25 28:26-27, Rom.15:21" (LXX), 2 Cor.10:12; with accusative of thing(s), Matt.13:23, 51, Luke.2:50 18:34 24:45; before ὅτι, Matt.16:12 17:13; before quæst. indir., Eph.5:17; ἐπὶ τ. ἄρτοις, Mark.6:52; as subst., συνίων (ὁ σ., WH, mg.), a man of understanding, i.e. in moral and religious sense, Rom.3:11 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4922.d:
συν-οδεύω 
 [in LXX: Zec.8:21 א1 (הָלַךְ), Tob.5:16 א, Wis.6:23 * ;] 
to journey with: with dative of person(s), Acts.9:7 (Plut., al.).†
 (AS)

G4923.d:
συνοδία, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Neh.7:5, 64 (יָחַשׂ) * ;] 
  1. a journey in company (Plut., al.). 
  2. By meton., κ company of travellers, a caravan: Luke.2:44.†
 (AS)

G4924.d:
συν-οικέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX for בַּעַל etc. ;] 
to dwell together: of man and wife (Hdt., al.), with dative of person(s), 1 Pet.3:7,†
 (AS)

G4925.d:
συν-οίκοδομέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: I Est.5:68 * ;] 
  1. to build together or with (with dative of person(s), 1Esdras, l.with). 
  2. Of various materials, to build up together (Thuc., al.): metaphorically, of Christians, Eph.2:22.†
 (AS)

G4926.d:
συν-ομιλέω, -ῶ 
 to converse with (absol., FlJ, Bl, v, 13, 1; before μετά, Cebes, 13): with dative of person(s), Acts.10:27.†
 (AS)

G4927.d:
συν-ομορέω, -ῶ 
 to border on: with dative, Acts.18:7 (Byz.).†
 (AS)

G4928.d:
συν-οχή, -ῆς, ή
 (συνέχω), [in LXX: Jdg.2:3 (?), Job.30:3 (שׁוֹא), Job.38:28 A; Mic.5:1 (4:14), Jer.52:5 (מָצוֹר) * ;] 
  1. a holding or being held together. 
  2. a narrow place (Hom., al.). Metaphorical, straits, distress: Luke.21:25; καρδίας, 2 Cor.2:4.†
 (AS)

G4929.d:
συν-τάσσω 
 [in LXX chiefly for צָוָה pi. ;] 
to prescribe, ordain, arrange: with dative of person(s), Matt.21:6 26:19 27:10" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G4930.d:
συντέλεια, -ας, ἡ
 (συντελέω), [in LXX chiefly for כָּלָה and (in Da) for קוּם ;] 
  1. in cl., a joint payment or contribution for public service; hence, generally, joint action (Plat.). 
  2. In late writers (Polyb., al.), consummation, completion: σ. τ. αἰῶνος, -ων (cf. Dan LXX TH Dan.12:13, al.), Matt.13:39-40, 49 24:3 28:20, Heb.9:26.†
 (AS)

G4931.d:
συν-τελέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX chiefly for כָּלָה pi., also for עָשָׂה, תָּמַם, etc. ;] 
"perfective" of τελέω (cf. M, Pr., 118), 
  1. to complete, finish, bring to an end: Luke.4:13; pass., Luke.4:2, John.2:3, WH, mg., Acts.21:27. 
  2. to effect, accomplish, bring to fulfilment (cf. MM, xxiv): Mark.13:4, Rom.9:28, Heb.8:8.†
 (AS)

G4932.d:
συν-τέμνω 
 [in LXX chiefly for חָרַץ ;] 
  1. to cut in pieces. 
  2. to cut down, cut short: metapb., λόγον, Rom.9:28 (LXX) (Hdt., Plat., Fur., al.).†
 (AS)

G4933.d:
συν-τηρέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Eze.18:19 (שָׁמַר), Da TH Dan.7:28 A (נְטַר), Sir.13:12 and freq., Tob.1:11, 2Ma.12:42, al. ;] 
"perfective" of τηρέω (see M, Pr., 113, 116), 
 to preserve, keep safe, keep close: with accusative of person(s), Mark.6:20; with accusative of thing(s), Matt.9:17; ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luke.2:19 (Arist. and later writers; cf. MM, xxiv).†

G4934.d:
συν-τίθημι 
 [in LXX: 1Ki.22:13 (קָשַׁר), etc. ;]

  (a) to observe, perceive; 
  (b) to determine, agree, covenant: with inf., Luke.22:5; before τοῦ, with inf., Acts.23:20; before ἵνα, John.9:22.†

 [in LXX for שִׁית, etc. ;]

  adv. (συντέμνω) [in LXX: Pro.13:23 23:28,  3Ma.5:25 * ;] 
concisely, briefly: Acts.24:4 (for a similar ex., see MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G4936.d:
συν-τρέχω

to run together or with: before ἐκεῖ, Mark.6:33; πρόσ, with accusative, Acts.3:11; metaphorically, 1 Pet.4:4.†
 (AS)

G4937.d:
συν-τρίβω 
 [in LXX chiefly for שָׁבַר ;] 
to shatter, break in pieces: Matt.12:20 (LXX), Mark.5:4 14:3, John.19:36" (LXX), Rev.2:27; of persons and parts of the body, to break, crush, bruise: Luke.9:39; figuratively, Rom.16:20.†
 (AS)

G4938.d:
σύν-τριμμα, -τος, τό

a fracture (Arist.; Le, l.with, al.). Metaphorical, calamity, destruction (Isa, l.with, Wis.3:3, al.): Rom.3:16" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G4939.d:
σύν-τροφος, -ου, ὁ

  1. prop., one nourished or brought up with, a foster-brother: Acts.13:1 EV. 
  2. In Hellenistic usage, as a court term, an intimate friend of a king (see Deiss., BS, 305, 310 f.): Acts.13:1 (cf. also MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G4940.d:
συν-τυγχάνω 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.8:14 * ;] 
to meet with, fall in with: with dative of person(s), Luke.8:19.†
 (AS)

G4942.d:
συν-υπο-κρίνομαι 
 to play a part with, dissemble with: with dative, Gal.2:13 (Polyb.).†
 (AS)

G4943.d:
συν-υπουργέω, -ῶ 
 to help together, join in serving: with dative instr., 2 Cor.1:11.†
 (AS)

G4944.d:
συν-ωδίνω 
 to be in travail together (Arist.): metapb. (Eur.), Rom.8:22.†
 (AS)

G4945.d:
συνωμοσία, -ας, ή
 (συνόμνυμι, to conspire), [in Sm.: Eze.22:25 * ;] 
a conspiracy: Acts.23:13.†
 (AS)

Σύρος, -ου, ὁ, fem. Σύρα 
 a Syrian: Luke.4:27, Mark.7:26, WH, mg.†

Συροφοινίκισσα (Rec. -φοίνισσα), -ης, ἡ

Σύρτις (L, σῦρτις), -εως, accusative -ιν, ἡ, 
 Syrtis, the name of two large sand-banks on the Libyan coast: Acts.27:17.†
 (AS)

σύρω 
 [in LXX: 4Ki.17:13 (סָחַב), 4Ma.6:1, al. ;] 
to draw, drag: with accusative of thing(s), John.21:8, Rev.12:4; with accusative of person(s), of taking to trial or punish­ment, Acts.8:3; ἔξω τ. πόλεως, Acts.14:19; ἐπὶ τ. πολιτάρχας (cf. 4Mac, l.with), Acts.17:6 (cf. κατα-ούρω).†
 (AS)

G4952.d:
συ-σπαράσσω 
 to convulse completely: with accusative of person(s), Mark.9:20, Luke.9:42 (cf. σπαράσσω).†
 (AS)

G4953.d:
σύσ-σημον (T, συν-), -ου, τό 
 (σῆμα), [in LXX: Jdg.20:38, 40 (מַשְׂאֵת), Isa.5:26 49:22 62:10 (נֵס) * ;] 
a fixed sign or signal: Mark.14:44. (Strab., Plut., al.; condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 492 f.) †
 (AS)

G4954.d:
σύν-σωμος (Rec. συσσ-), -ον 
 (σῶμα), 
of the same body: Eph.3:6 (Eccl.).†
 (AS)

 (στασιάζω, to stir up sedition, Jdth.7:15, 2Ma.4:30 2Mac 14:6 *) 
= Att.. στασιώτης, 
 a rebel, revolutionist, one who stirs up sedition: Mark.15:7 (FlJ, al.).†
 συ-στασιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ, 
 a fellow-rioter: Mark.15:7, Rec.†
 (AS)

G4956.d:
συ-στατικός (Tr. συν-), -ή, -όν 
 (συνίστημι), 
  1. for putting together, constructive. 
  2. for bringing together, introductory, commendatory: ἐπιστολή (Arist., Diog. L., al.; and see MM, xxiv), 2 Cor.3:1.†
 (AS)

G4957.d:
συν-σταυρόω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ, 
 to crucify together with: pass., with dative, John.19:32; id. before σύν, Matt.27:44, Mark.15:32. Metaphorical, of the mystical death of the Christian with Christ: Rom.6:6, Gal.2:20 (Eccl.).†
 (AS)

G4958.d:
συν-στέλλω
 (Rec. συσ-), [in LXX: Jdg.8:28 11:33 (כָּנַע ni.), Sir.4:31, al. ;] 
  1. to draw together, contract, shorten: of time, 1 Cor.7:29. 
  2. to wrap up: of enshrouding a body for burial (Eur.), with accusative, Acts.5:6.†
 (AS)

G4959.d:
συν-στενάζω (Rec. συσ-), 
 to groan together or with: Rom.8:22 (with dative of person(s), Eur., Ion., 935).†
 (AS)

G4960.d:
συν-στοιχέω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ, 
 to stand in the same rank or line (Polyb). Metaphorical, to correspond to: Gal.4:25 (see Lft., in l).†
 (AS)

G4961.d:
συν-στρατιώτης (Rec. συσ-), -ου, ὁ 
 a fellow-soldier (Plat., Xen., al.). Metaphorical, of fellowship in Christian service: Phil.2:25, Phm 2 .†
 (AS)

G4962.d:
συ-στέφω 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָשַׁר ;] 
  1. to twist together: with accusative of thing(s), Acts.28:3. 
  2. Pass., of persons, to gather themselves together: Matt.17:22 (WH, R, mg.).†
 (AS)

G4963.d:
συ-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (συστρέφω), [in LXX: Rom.4:19 13:12 (צָרַר); σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Amo.7:10 (קָשַׁר), etc. ;] 
  1. a twisting together (Plat.). 
  2. a concourse, a riotous gathering (Polyb.): Acts.19:40; σ. ποιεῖσθαι (Am, l.with), to make a compact (RV, banded themselves together): Acts.23:12.†
 (AS)

G4964.d:
συν-σχηματιζω (Rec. συσ-), 
 (σχῆμα), 
to conform to (Arist.). Pass., to be conformed to, conform oneself to: Rom.12:2, 1 Pet.1:14.†
 (AS)

G4965.d:
Συχάρ
 (Ε, Σιχάρ), indecl., ἡ 
Sychar, a town of Samaria: John.4:5.†
 (AS)

G4966.d:
Συχέμ  indecl. (Heb. שְׁכֶם), 
 Shechem; 
  1. the son of Hamor (Gen.33:19): Acts.7:16 b, Rec. 
  2. A city of Samaria (AV, Sychem; in LXX also sometimes Σίκιμα, -ων, as in FlJ): Acts.7:16 a,b.†
 (AS)

G4967.d:
σφαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (σφάζω), [in LXX for טָבַח, הֲרֵגָה, etc. ;] 
slaughter: Acts.8:32 (LXX); πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Rom.8:36 (LXX); ἡμέρα σφαγῆς, Jas.5:5.†
 (AS)

G4968.d:
σφάγιον, -ου, τό
 (σφαγή), [in LXX: Amo.5:25 (זֶבַח), Eze.21:10, 15 21:28 (טֶבַח), Lev.22:23 (נְדָבָה) * ;] 
a victim for slaughter: Acts.7:42 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4969.d:
σφάζω 
 [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַט ;] 
to slay, slaughter (esp. of victims for sacrifice): ἀρνίον, Rev.5:6, 12 13:8; of persons, 1 John.3:12, Rev.5:9 6:4, 9 18:24; ἐσφαγμένη εἰς θάνατον (RV, smitten unto death), Rev.13:3 (cf. κατα-σφάζω).†
 (AS)

G4970.d:
σφόδρα  adv. (prop. neut. of σφοδρός, excessive, violent) 
 [in LXX chiefly for מְאֹד ;] 
very, very much, exceedingly: with verbs, Matt.17:6, 23 18:31 19:25 26:22 27:54, Acts.6:7; with adjectives, Matt.2:10, Mark.16:4, Luke.18:23, Rev.16:21.†
 (AS)

G4973.d:
σφραγίς, -ῖδος, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Exod.28:11, al. (חוֹתָם) Exod.35:22 (חָח), Sir.17:22, al. ;] 
  1. a seal, signet: Rev.7:2. 
  2. The impression of a seal or signet, a seal (on its various purposes, see: σφραγίζω): on a book or roll, Rev.5:1-2, 5 5:9 6:1, 3 6:5, 7 6:9, 12 8:1; metaphorically, Rom.4:11, 1 Cor.9:2, 2 Tim.2:19, Rev.9:4.†
 (AS)

G4974.d:
σφυρόν, -οῦ, τό, 
 [in LXX: Job.41:21 (לָהַט) * ;] 
the ankle: Acts.3:7, Rec. (T, WH, σφυδρόν; see Bl., § 6, 8).†
 (AS)

G4975.d:
σχέδον
  adv. (ἔχω), [in LXX: 2Ma.5:2, 3Ma.5:14 3Mac 5:45 * ;] 
  1. of place, near. 
  2. Of degree, almost, nearly: Acts.13:44 19:26, Heb.9:22.†
 (AS)

G4976.d:
σχῆμα, -τος, τό
 (ἔχω), [in LXX: Isa.3:17 (פֹּת) * ;] 
figure, fashion: 1 Cor.7:31, Phil.2:8.†
 SYN.: see: μορφή  (AS)

G4977.d:
σχίζω 
 [in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע ;] 
to cleave, rend: Matt.27:51, Mark.1:10 15:38, Luke.5:36 23:45, John.19:24 21:11; metaphorically, in pass., to be divided into factions, Acts.14:4 23:7.† 
 (AS)

G4978.d:
σχίσμα, -τος, τό
 (σχίζω), 
a rent (Arist., al.): Matt.9:16, Mark.2:21. Metaphorical, a dissension, division: John.7:43 9:16 10:19, 1 Cor.1:10 11:18 12:25.†
 SYN.: see: αἵρεσις  (AS)

G4979.d:
σχοινίον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of σχοῖνος, a rush), 
[in LXX chiefly for a rope (prop., one made of rushes): John.2:15, Acts.27:32.†
 (AS)

G4980.d:
σχολάζω
 (σχολή), [in LXX: Exod.5:8, 17, Ps.46:10 (רָפָה ni., hi.) * ;] 
to be at leisure, hence, to have time or opportunity for, to devote oneself to, be occupied in: 1 Cor.7:5; of things, to be unoccupied, empty (Plut., Eur., al.): οἶκος, Matt.12:44, Luke.11:25 (T [WH], R, om.).†
 (AS)

G4981.d:
σχολή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Gen.33:14 (κατὰ σ., אַט), Pro.28:19, Sir.38:24 * ;] 
  1. leisure. 
  2. Later (from Plato on), 
  (a) that for which leisure is employed, a disputation, lecture; 
  (b) the place where lectures are delivered, a school: Acts.19:9 (for the later sense of employment, see MM, xxiv).†
 (AS)

G4982.d:
σώζω (on the more accurate σῴζω, see WH, Intr., §410; Bl., §3, 1-3), 
 [in LXX chiefly for ישׁע hi., also for מלט ni., נצל ni., etc. ;] 
to save from peril, injury or suffering: Matt.8:25, Mark.13:20, Luke.23:35, al.; τ. ψυχήν, Matt.16:25, al.; before ἐκ, John.12:27, Heb.5:7, Ju 5; of healing, restoring to health: Matt.9:22, Mark.5:34, al. In NT, esp. of salvation from spiritual disease and death, in which sense it is "spoken of in Scripture as either (1) past, (2) present, or (3) future, according as redemption, grace, or glory is the point in view. Thus (1) Rom.8:24, Eph.2:5, 8 2 Tim.1:9, Titus.3:5; (2) Acts.2:47, 1 Cor.1:18, 15:2, 2 Cor.2:15; (3) Matt.10:22, Rom.13:11, Phil.2:12, Heb.9:28" (Vau. on Rom.5:9). Seq. ἀπό, Matt.1:21, Acts.2:40, Rom.5:9; ἐκ, Jas.5:20, Ju 23 (cf. Cremer, 532ff.). 
 (AS)

G4983.d:
σῶμα, -τος, τό, 
 [in LXX for גְּוִיָּה ,בָּשָׂר, etc., and for Aram. נְבֵלָה ;] 
a body. 
  1. Prop., of the human body, 
  (a) as always in Hom. (opposite to δέμας), of the dead body: Matt.27:58, 59 Mark.15:43, al.; 
  (b) of the living body: Luke.11:34, 1 Cor.6:13, al.; ἐν σ. εἶναι, Heb.13:3; as the instrument of the soul, τὰ διὰ τοῦ σ., 2 Cor.5:10; opposite to πνεῦμα, Rom.8:10, 1 Cor.5:3 7:4, Jas.2:26; to ψυχή, Matt.6:25 10:28, Luke.12:22 (cf. Wis.1:1, al.); to τὸ π. καὶ ἡ ψ., 1 Thess.5:23; σ. ψυχικόν, opposite to σ. πνευματικόν, 1 Cor.15:44; ὁ ναὸς τοῦ σ. αὐτοῦ (genitive epexeg.), John.2:21; τὸ σ. τ. ταπεινώσεως (Hebraistic "genitive of definition"; M, Pr., 73f.; Bl., §35, 5), opposite to τὸ σ. τ. δοξῆς αὐτοῦ, Phil.3:21; similarly, τὸ σ. τ. σαρκός, Col.1:22; σ. τοῦ θανάτου (subject to death), Rom.7:24; σ. τ. ἁμαρτίας, Rom.6:6; 
  (with) periphr., ἀνθρώπου, then absol., σῶμα (Soph., Xen., al.), a person, and in later writers (Polyb., al.), a slave: Rev.18:13 (cf. MM, i, ii, xxiv; Deiss., BS, 160). 
  2. Of the bodies of animals: living, Jas.3:3; dead, Heb.13:11 ( Exod.29:14, al.). 
  3. Of inanimate objects (cf. Eng. "heavenly bodies"): 1 Cor.15:37, 38 40 (Diod., al.). 
  4. Of any corporeal substance (Plat., al.): opposite to σκιά, Col.2:17. Metaphorical, of a number of persons united by a common bond; in NT, of the Church as the spiritual body of Christ: Rom.12:5, 1 Cor.10:16, 17 12:13, 27, Eph.1:23 2:16 4:4, 12, 16 5:23, 30, Col.1:18, 24 2:19 3:15; ἓν σ. κ. ἓν πνεῦμα, Eph.4:4. 
 (AS)

G4984.d:
σωματικός, -ή, -όν
 (σῶμα), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 4Mac 3:1 * ;] 
  (a) of or for the body, bodily: γυμνασία, 1 Tim.4:8; 
  (b) (opposite to ἀσώματος) bodily, corporeal: εἶδος, Luke.3:22.†
 (AS)

G4985.d:
σωματικῶς 
 adv., 
bodily, corporeally: Col.2:9 (see ICC, Lft., in l).†
 (AS)

G4987.d:
σωρεύω 
 [in LXX: Pro.25:22 (חָתָה), Jdth.15:11 * ;] 
  (a) to heap on: with accusative before ἐπί with accusative, Rom.12:20 (LXX) (Arist., al.); 
  (b) to heap with: with accusative and dative, metaphorically, ἁμαρτίαις, 2 Tim.3:6 (overwhelmed with, Field, Notes, 217) (Polyb.).†
 (AS)

G4990.d:
σωτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
 (σώζω), [in LXX for יָשַׁע and cognate forms ;] 
saviour, deliverer, preserver, a frequently epithet of kings in the Ptolemaic and Rom. periods (Deiss., BS, 83; LAE, 368 f.; MM, xxiv), in NT, 
  (a) of God (as LXX: Ps.24:5, Isa.12:2, al.): Luke.1:47, 1 Tim.1:1 2:3 4:10, Titus.1:3 2:10 3:4, Ju 25; 
  (b) of Christ: Luke.2:11, Acts.5:31 13:23, Phil.3:20; τ. κόσμου, John.4:42, 1 John.4:14 (for the general use of the word, see Westc., in l); ἡμῶν, 2 Tim.1:10, Titus.1:4 3:6; θεὸς (κύριος) καὶ σ. (see Deiss., LAE, 348.4; M, Pr., 84), Titus.2:13, 2 Pet.1:1 1:11 2:20 3:2 3:18; σ. τοῦ σώματος (i.e. of the Church; see: σῶμα, 5), Eph.5:23.†
 (AS)

G4991.d:
σωτηρία, -ας, ἡ
 (σωτήρ), [in LXX for יֶשַׁע, יְשׁוּעָה, תְּשׁוּעָה, פְּלֵיטָה, etc. ;] 
deliverance, preservation, salvation, safety (Lat. salus): Acts.7:25 27:34, Heb.11:7; ἐξ ἐχθρῶν, Luke.1:71. In NT esp. of Messianic and spiritual salvation (see: σώζω): Luke.19:9, John.4:22, Acts.4:12 13:47, Rom.11:11,  2 Thess.2:13, 2 Tim.3:15, Heb.2:3 6:9, 2 Pet.3:15, Ju 3; opposite to ἀπηώλεια, Phil.1:28; αἰώνιος-., Heb.5:9; ὁ λόγος (τὸ εὐαγγέλιον) τῆς σ., Acts.13:26, Eph.1:13; ὁδὸς σωτηρίας, Acts.16:17; κέρας σωτηρίας, Luke.1:69; ἡμέρα σωτηρίας, 2 Cor.6:2 (LXX); κατεργάζεσθαι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σ., Phil.2:12; κληρονομεῖν σ., Heb.1:14; ὁ ἀρχηγὸς τῆς σ., Heb.2:10; εἰς σ., Rom.1:16 10:1, 10, 1 Pet.2:2; σ. as a present possession (see: σώζω), Luke.1:77, 2 Cor.1:6 7:10, Phil.1:19, 2 Tim.2:10; as more fully realized in the future: Rom.13:11, 1 Thess.5:8-9, Heb.9:28, 1 Pet.1:5 1:9-10, Rev.7:10 12:10 19:1.†
 (AS)

G4992.d:
σωτήριος, -ον
 (σωτήρ), [in LXX for יְשׁוּעָה, שֶׁלֶם, etc. ;] 
saving, bringing salvation, in NT always in spiritual sense (see: σώζω, σωτηρία): ἡ χάρις ἡ σ., Titus.2:1. Neut., -τὸ σ., as subst. (cl.), salvation: Luke.2:30; τ. σ. τ. θεοῦ, Luke.3:6, Acts.28:28; περικεφαλαίαν τοῦ σ., Eph.6:17.†
 (AS)

G4993.d:
σωφρονέω, -ῶ
 (σώφρων), 
  (a) to be of sound mind or in one's right mind: Mark.5:15, Luke.8:35; opposite to ἐκστῆναι, 2 Cor.5:13 (Hdt.); 
  (b) to be temperate, discreet, self-controlled (opposite to μαίνεσθαι, ὑβρίζειν, etc.; sch., Thuc., al.): Titus.2:6; opposite to ὑπερφρονεῖν, Rom.12:3; σ. καὶ νήφειν, 1 Pet.4:7.†
 (AS)

G4994.d:
σωφρονίζω 
 [in Aq.: Isa.38:16 * ;] 
to make σώφρων, recall one to his senses, control (RV, train): with accusative of person(s), Titus.2:4.†
 (AS)

G4995.d:
σωφρονισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (σωφρονίζω), 
  (a) an admonishing (F1J, Plut., al.); 
  (b) self-control, self-discipline: 2 Tim.1:7 (on the reflexive meaning here, see Ellic., in l).†
 (AS)

G4996.d:
σωφρόνως 
 adv., [in LXX: Wis.9:11 * ;] 
with sound mind, prudently, soberly: Titus.2:12.†
 (AS)

G4997.d:
σωφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Est.3:13, Wis.8:7, 2Ma.4:37, 4Ma.6:1-35 * ;] 
  (a) soundness of mind, good sense, sanity (opposite to μανία, Xen.): Acts.26:25; 
  (b) self-control, sobriety: 1 Tim.2:9 (see Tr., Syn., § xx), 1 Tim.2:15.†
 (AS)

G4998.d:
σώφρων, -ον 
 [in LXX: 4Ma.9:1-32 * ;] 
  (a) of sound mind, sane, sensible; 
  (b) self-controlled, sober-minded: 1 Tim.3:2, Titus.1:8 2:2, 5 (Arist.).†
 (AS)

G4999.d:
ταβέρνη
 (Lat. taberna), see: Τρεῖς Ταβέρναι. 
Τρεῖς Ταβέρναι 
 (see: ταβέρνη), 
Three Taverns (Lit. Tres Tabernae) a halting place on the Appian Way: Acts.28:15 (see DB, iv, 690).†
 (AS)
